dinners.title: Blackstone smashburgers
dinners.subtitle: Two crispy-edged smashed patties, melted cheese, dill pickles and shredded lettuce on a toasted bun.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two. While it heats, divide the 2 lb of beef into 10 loose balls, a little over 3 oz each. Don’t pack them tight. Shred the romaine heart and set out the cheese, pickles and buns.

Set 5 balls on the hot griddle a few inches apart (two rounds keeps it calm). Press each one flat and thin with a sturdy spatula, leaning on it for 10 seconds, then season with a pinch of the salt and pepper. Cook without moving until the edges are deep brown and crisp, 2–3 minutes.

Scrape under each patty so the crust comes with it, flip, and lay a cheese slice on every other patty. Cook 1–2 minutes more, until a thermometer slid in from the side reads 160°F. Move them to a plate and cook the other 5 balls the same way.
Toast the buns cut side down on a clean part of the griddle until golden, about 1 minute.

steps: Spread the buns with the mustard and ketchup. Stack two patties on each, the cheese one on top, and finish with pickles and a handful of shredded lettuce.
tips: Cold beef smashes best: keep the balls in the fridge until the griddle is hot.
Smash once, in the first 30 seconds. Pressing later squeezes the juice out.
dinners.leftovers: Cooked patties keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat in a covered skillet with a splash of water for 2–3 minutes.
dinners.photo: A double smashburger with two thin, crispy-edged beef patties, melted cheddar, dill pickle chips and shredded lettuce on a toasted bun, on a plate beside golden french fries.

dinners.title: Griddled onion burgers
dinners.subtitle: Paper-thin onions smashed into double beef patties and caramelized under melted cheese.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two. While it heats, peel the onions and slice them as thin as you can; you want a big pile. Divide the 2 lb of beef into 10 loose balls, a little over 3 oz each.

Set 5 balls on the griddle, pile a handful of the onions on each and smash hard with a sturdy spatula so they press into the meat and start to cook. Season with a pinch of the salt and pepper and cook until the bottoms are deep brown, 2–3 minutes.

Flip so the onions are underneath, where they soften and caramelize against the griddle. Lay a cheese slice on every other patty and cook 2 minutes more, until the onions are golden and a thermometer slid in from the side reads 160°F. Repeat with the other 5 balls.
Toast the buns cut side down on a clean part of the griddle until golden, about 1 minute.

steps: Spread the buns with the mustard and stack two onion patties on each, the cheese one on top, with the pickles.
tips: Thin is the whole trick: paper-thin onions cook soft and sweet in the time the patty takes.
If any onions escape, push them into a pile next to the patties to brown, then spoon them on top.
dinners.leftovers: Cooked patties keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat in a covered skillet with a splash of water for 2–3 minutes.
dinners.photo: A double cheeseburger with caramelized paper-thin onions pressed into crispy beef patties, melted cheddar and pickles on a toasted bun, plated with french fries.

dinners.title: Green chile cheeseburgers
dinners.subtitle: Thick sirloin burgers with melted cheese, pickled jalapeños, crisp lettuce and a cool lime-yogurt spread.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two. While it heats, stir the yogurt with the zest and juice of the lime and put it in the fridge. Chop the jalapeños (use half for milder burgers) and shred the romaine heart.

Season the 6 frozen patties on both sides with the salt and pepper and set them on the hot griddle straight from the freezer (no thawing). Cook 5–6 minutes, flip once, and cook 5–6 minutes more, until a thermometer slid in from the side reads 160°F and the juices run clear.
Lay a cheese slice on each patty for the last minute so it melts, and toast the buns cut side down on a clean part of the griddle until golden.

steps: Spread the buns with the lime yogurt, add a patty and top with jalapeños and shredded lettuce. Six burgers: one each, and one to split for whoever is hungriest.
tips: Put the jalapeños in a bowl on the table so everyone picks their own heat.
Keep the patties frozen until the griddle is hot; they hold their shape better.
dinners.leftovers: Cooked patties keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat in a covered skillet with a splash of water for 2–3 minutes.
dinners.photo: A thick grilled sirloin burger with melted cheese, bright green pickled jalapeño slices, shredded lettuce and a creamy white spread on a toasted bun, plated with french fries.

dinners.title: Mushroom melt burgers
dinners.subtitle: Thick sirloin burgers under a big pile of garlicky browned mushrooms and melted cheese.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two. Mince the 2 garlic cloves while it heats.

Season the 6 frozen patties on both sides with the salt and pepper and set them on the hot griddle straight from the freezer (no thawing). Cook 5–6 minutes, flip once, and cook 5–6 minutes more, until a thermometer slid in from the side reads 160°F and the juices run clear.

As soon as the patties are on, melt the butter on another part of the griddle and spread out the 16 oz of mushrooms. Leave them alone for 2 minutes, then stir now and then until they are browned and their liquid has cooked off, 6–8 minutes. Stir in the garlic for the last minute.
Pile the mushrooms on the patties, top each with a cheese slice and let it melt, about 1 minute. Toast the buns cut side down on a clean part of the griddle.

steps: Spread the buns with the mustard and add a mushroom-cheese patty to each. Six burgers: one each, and one to split for whoever is hungriest.
tips: Don’t salt the mushrooms until they are brown; salt pulls out water and they steam instead.
Not a mushroom fan at the table? Leave one patty plain before you pile them on.
dinners.leftovers: Cooked patties keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat in a covered skillet with a splash of water for 2–3 minutes.
dinners.photo: A thick sirloin burger smothered in browned sliced mushrooms and melted cheese on a toasted bun, plated with french fries.

dinners.title: BBQ slaw burgers
dinners.subtitle: Thick sirloin burgers brushed with barbecue sauce under melted cheese and a big pile of crunchy, tangy slaw.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two. While it heats, toss the 14 oz bag of coleslaw mix with the yogurt, the cider vinegar and 1 tablespoon of the barbecue sauce, and put it in the fridge.

Season the 6 frozen patties on both sides with the salt and pepper and set them on the hot griddle straight from the freezer (no thawing). Cook 5–6 minutes, flip once, and cook 5–6 minutes more, until a thermometer slid in from the side reads 160°F and the juices run clear.
Brush the tops with the remaining barbecue sauce for the last 2 minutes, lay a cheese slice on each and let it melt. Toast the buns cut side down on a clean part of the griddle.

steps: Fill each bun with a saucy patty and a tall pile of slaw; serve the rest of the slaw on the side. Six burgers: one each, and one to split for whoever is hungriest.
tips: Sauce goes on at the end: barbecue sauce burns if it sits on the hot griddle.
The slaw is better after 10 minutes in the fridge, so make it first.
dinners.leftovers: Cooked patties keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat in a covered skillet with a splash of water for 2–3 minutes.
dinners.photo: A thick sirloin burger glazed with dark barbecue sauce, melted cheese and creamy crunchy coleslaw on a toasted bun, plated with french fries.

dinners.title: Dill pickle burgers
dinners.subtitle: Thick sirloin burgers with a tangy chopped-pickle mustard sauce, crisp lettuce and extra pickles.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two. While it heats, finely chop half the pickles and stir them into the yogurt and mustard. Shred the romaine heart.

Season the 6 frozen patties on both sides with the salt and pepper and set them on the hot griddle straight from the freezer (no thawing). Cook 5–6 minutes, flip once, and cook 5–6 minutes more, until a thermometer slid in from the side reads 160°F and the juices run clear.
Lay a cheese slice on each patty for the last minute so it melts, and toast the buns cut side down on a clean part of the griddle until golden.

steps: Spread the buns with the pickle sauce and add a patty, the remaining pickles and shredded lettuce. Six burgers: one each, and one to split for whoever is hungriest.
tips: Pat the pickles dry before chopping so the sauce stays thick.
dinners.leftovers: Cooked patties keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat in a covered skillet with a splash of water for 2–3 minutes.
dinners.photo: A thick sirloin burger with melted cheese, dill pickles, shredded lettuce and a creamy chopped-pickle mustard sauce on a toasted bun, plated with french fries.

dinners.title: Sticky orange chicken
dinners.subtitle: Crispy-edged chicken thighs seared on the griddle and tossed in a glossy fresh-orange, garlic and ginger glaze.
steps: Zest one orange, then juice all three; you want about 1 cup. In a small saucepan whisk the juice and zest with the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, the 3 minced garlic cloves, the grated ginger and 1 tablespoon of the cornstarch until no lumps are left.
Cut the chicken thighs into 1-inch pieces, sprinkle with the salt and toss with the remaining 2 tablespoons of cornstarch until every piece is lightly coated.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.

Spread the oil over the griddle and add the chicken in a single layer with space between the pieces. Turn every couple of minutes until browned and crisp at the edges and the thickest pieces read 165°F, 8–10 minutes.
While the chicken cooks, bring the sauce to a simmer over medium heat, whisking, and cook until it is thick and glossy enough to coat a spoon, 1–2 minutes.

steps: Toss the hot chicken with the glaze in a large bowl and serve right away, while the edges are still crisp.
tips: No Blackstone tonight? A large skillet over medium-high works; cook the chicken in two batches so it browns instead of steaming.
Whisk the sauce again right before heating: cornstarch settles to the bottom.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat in a skillet with a splash of water so the glaze loosens.
dinners.photo: Bite-size crispy chicken pieces coated in a shiny amber orange glaze with thin strips of orange zest, piled in a white bowl.

dinners.title: Chicken tikka masala
dinners.subtitle: Browned chicken and sweet peas simmered in a creamy, mild tikka masala sauce.
steps: Cut the chicken breasts into 1½-inch pieces, pat them dry with paper towels and season with the salt.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Brown the chicken in two batches, 2–3 minutes per side; it only needs color now, because it finishes cooking in the sauce. Return all of it to the pan.

steps: Pour in both jars of tikka masala simmer sauce (Maya Kaimal, or the Patak’s on the shelf; they are fully seasoned, so nothing else goes in). Swirl ¼ cup of water in the jars and add that too.

steps.text: Bring to a gentle bubble, then cover, turn the heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring now and then, until the thickest pieces of chicken read 165°F, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the 8 oz of frozen peas and simmer 2 minutes more, until they are hot and bright green.

tips: Start the rice before the chicken: both are done at about the same time.
Warm naan is a good swap for the rice when you want something to scoop with.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge in a covered container; it freezes well for 3 months and reheats gently in a saucepan.
dinners.photo: Chunks of chicken and green peas in a rich orange, creamy tikka masala sauce in a shallow bowl beside golden turmeric rice.

dinners.title: Chicken lo mein
dinners.subtitle: Garlicky soy-sesame noodles tossed with sliced chicken and a big pile of cabbage and carrots.

steps.text: Fill your largest pot with about 5 quarts of water, add 1 tablespoon of the salt, cover and bring to a full rolling boil over high heat. It takes 10–15 minutes, so start it first. While it heats, slice the chicken thighs into thin strips, cut the carrots into matchsticks, and whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, the 4 minced garlic cloves and the grated ginger in a small bowl.

Add the 12 oz of spaghetti (three-quarters of a 1 lb box) to the boiling water, stir for the first minute so it doesn’t stick, and boil uncovered until tender with a little bite, 8–10 minutes (check the box). Take it out a minute early; it cooks a little more on the griddle. Drain.
Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Spread the oil on the griddle and cook the chicken in a single layer, turning, until browned and the thickest strips read 165°F, 5–7 minutes. Push it to a cooler part of the griddle.

Stir-fry the carrots and the whole 14 oz bag of coleslaw mix on the hot part until just tender, 2–3 minutes. Add the noodles and the sauce and fold everything together with the chicken until glossy and steaming, about 2 minutes.

tips: Two wide spatulas make tossing noodles on the griddle easy.
Indoors, use your largest skillet and cook the chicken first, then the vegetables, then toss in the noodles.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat in a skillet with a splash of water.
dinners.photo: Glossy brown lo mein noodles tossed with strips of chicken, shredded cabbage and carrot matchsticks, piled high on a platter.

dinners.title: Chicken fried rice
dinners.subtitle: Hibachi-style jasmine rice griddled with egg, chicken and plenty of colorful vegetables.

steps.text: Rinse the 1½ cups of jasmine rice in a fine strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium saucepan with 2¼ cups of water and ½ teaspoon of the salt and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid, then take it off the heat and leave it covered 10 minutes more. Fluff with a fork. Spread it on a large platter to steam off and cool while you prep; dry rice fries, wet rice clumps.

steps: Cut the chicken thighs into ½-inch pieces, mince the 3 garlic cloves and beat the 4 eggs in a bowl.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Spread 1 tablespoon of the oil on the griddle and cook the chicken, turning, until browned and the thickest pieces read 165°F, 6–8 minutes. Move it to a cooler part of the griddle.
Cook the 1½ lb of frozen mixed vegetables on the hot part until hot and dry, 3–4 minutes. Push them aside, add the remaining oil and scramble the eggs until just set.

Melt the butter on the hot part, add the rice and garlic and let it sizzle untouched for a minute so it toasts. Fold in the chicken, vegetables, eggs, soy sauce and sesame oil and toss until hot all the way through, 2–3 minutes.

tips: Day-old rice from the fridge makes the best fried rice; cook it the night before if you remember.
Break up clumps of rice with the edge of the spatula before the soy sauce goes on.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; cool it within an hour of cooking and reheat in a hot skillet until steaming.
dinners.photo: A heaping plate of golden fried jasmine rice with scrambled egg, diced chicken, peas, carrots and corn, glistening with soy and sesame.

dinners.title: Beef & broccoli noodles
dinners.subtitle: Soy-ginger glazed lean beef and lots of broccoli tangled through garlicky noodles.

steps.text: Fill your largest pot with about 5 quarts of water, add 1 tablespoon of the salt, cover and bring to a full rolling boil over high heat. It takes 10–15 minutes, so start it first. While it heats, whisk the soy sauce, honey, cornstarch, sesame oil and ½ cup of water in a small bowl. Mince the 4 garlic cloves and grate the ginger.

Add the 12 oz of spaghetti (three-quarters of a 1 lb box) to the boiling water, stir for the first minute so it doesn’t stick, and boil uncovered until tender with a little bite, 9–11 minutes (check the box). Add the 2 lb of frozen broccoli to the pot for the last 2 minutes. Scoop out 1 cup of the cooking water with a mug, then drain.

Set a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 2 lb of ground beef and break it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon as it cooks. Keep going until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 160°F, 8–10 minutes. Tip the pan and spoon off any liquid fat.
Stir the garlic and ginger into the beef for 30 seconds, until you can smell them. Whisk the sauce again, pour it in and simmer until it thickens, about 1 minute.

steps: Add the noodles and broccoli and toss with tongs, loosening with splashes of the saved water, until everything is glossy.
tips: Start browning the beef when the noodles go in and both finish together.
The broccoli goes straight from the freezer into the pasta water; no thawing.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat with a splash of water in a skillet or the microwave.
dinners.photo: Noodles tossed with browned ground beef crumbles and bright green broccoli florets in a glossy dark soy-ginger glaze, in a wide bowl.

dinners.title: Peanut-lime chicken wraps
dinners.subtitle: Grilled chicken, crunchy cabbage and a tangy peanut-lime sauce rolled in warm tortillas.

steps.text: Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Lay the chicken breasts between two sheets of plastic wrap (or in a zip bag) and pound the thick ends with a rolling pin or the bottom of a pan until each is an even ¾ inch thick, so they cook through without drying out. Rub them with the oil and 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce. Grill, turning once halfway, until marked and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F: 10–14 minutes on an open grill, 6–8 minutes if yours closes like a press. Move to a clean plate, rest 5 minutes so the juices stay in, then slice thin.

steps: While the chicken cooks, whisk the peanut butter, the juice of both limes, the remaining soy sauce, the honey, the 2 minced garlic cloves and 3–4 tablespoons of warm water into a smooth sauce that drizzles off a spoon. Shred the carrots and toss them with the coleslaw mix.

steps.text: Warm the tortillas two or three at a time in a dry skillet over medium-high heat, 20–30 seconds per side, until soft with a few toasted spots. Stack them inside a clean kitchen towel so they stay warm and bendy.

steps: Fill each tortilla with a big handful of the slaw and some chicken, spoon over the peanut sauce and roll up. Two wraps per person.
tips: Peanut sauce too thick? Whisk in warm water a spoonful at a time.
Set everything out and let each person build their own.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; store the chicken, slaw and sauce separately and roll fresh wraps for lunch.
dinners.photo: Flour tortilla wraps cut in half to show sliced grilled chicken, crunchy shredded cabbage and carrots with a creamy peanut sauce drizzle, on a plate with lime wedges.

dinners.title: Ginger chicken lettuce cups
dinners.subtitle: Crisp romaine cups filled with ginger-soy ground chicken, cabbage and shredded carrots.
steps: Pull the 3 romaine hearts apart into whole leaves, rinse and pat dry. Shred the carrots, grate the ginger and mince the 4 garlic cloves.

steps.text: Heat the oil in your largest skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 2.25 lb of ground chicken and break it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon as it cooks. Keep going until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 165°F, 8–10 minutes.

Stir in the ginger and garlic for 30 seconds. Add the coleslaw mix, carrots, soy sauce, honey and rice vinegar and toss until the cabbage just softens but still has some crunch, 3–4 minutes. Drizzle with the sesame oil.

steps: Bring the skillet to the table with the romaine leaves. Spoon the warm filling into the leaves and eat them like tacos.
tips: The sturdy inner leaves make the best cups; chop the floppy outer ones into the filling.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; the filling is good over rice or noodles the next day.
dinners.photo: Crisp romaine lettuce leaves filled with glossy ginger-soy ground meat, shredded cabbage and carrots, arranged on a platter.

dinners.title: Honey-ginger chicken noodles
dinners.subtitle: Golden chicken and plenty of bell pepper strips in a sticky honey-ginger glaze over noodles.

steps.text: Fill your largest pot with about 5 quarts of water, add 1 tablespoon of the salt, cover and bring to a full rolling boil over high heat. It takes 10–15 minutes, so start it first. While it heats, whisk the honey, soy sauce, cornstarch, grated ginger, the 4 minced garlic cloves and ⅓ cup of water. Cut the chicken thighs into 1-inch pieces and the 3 peppers into strips.

Add the 12 oz of spaghetti (three-quarters of a 1 lb box) to the boiling water, stir for the first minute so it doesn’t stick, and boil uncovered until tender with a little bite, 9–11 minutes (check the box). Scoop out 1 cup of the cooking water with a mug, then drain.

Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Cook the chicken in two batches so it browns, turning, until the thickest pieces read 165°F, 6–8 minutes per batch. Move it to a plate.
Add the peppers to the same skillet and stir-fry until they are bright and just tender, 2–3 minutes. Return the chicken, whisk the sauce again, pour it in and simmer until sticky, about 1 minute.

steps: Add the noodles and toss, loosening with splashes of the saved water, until everything is coated.
tips: Don’t crowd the chicken: a single layer browns, a pile steams.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat with a splash of water.
dinners.photo: Noodles tossed with golden chicken pieces and red and yellow bell pepper strips in a sticky honey-ginger glaze, in a large shallow bowl.

dinners.title: Steak & egg fried rice
dinners.subtitle: Takeout-style jasmine fried rice with seared bites of lean sirloin tip, egg and lots of mixed vegetables.

steps.text: Rinse the 1½ cups of jasmine rice in a fine strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium saucepan with 2¼ cups of water and ½ teaspoon of the salt and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid, then take it off the heat and leave it covered 10 minutes more. Fluff with a fork. Spread it on a large platter to cool while you prep; dry rice fries, wet rice clumps.

steps: Trim any silvery skin off the 1¾ lb of sirloin tip, cut the meat into ½-inch dice and toss with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce. Grate the ginger, mince the 3 garlic cloves and beat the 4 eggs.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Cook the steak in a single layer, turning once or twice, until browned and a thermometer in a thick piece reads 145°F, 3–4 minutes. Move it to a cooler part of the griddle.

Spread half the oil on the hot part and stir-fry the 1½ lb of frozen vegetables with the ginger and garlic until hot and dry, 3–4 minutes. Push them aside, add the remaining oil and scramble the eggs until just set.
Add the rice to the hot part and toss everything together with the remaining soy sauce and the sesame oil until steaming hot all the way through, 2–3 minutes.

tips: Day-old rice from the fridge makes the best fried rice.
Sirloin tip is lean: small dice and a hot, fast sear keep it tender, and it cuts most easily while it is still a little frozen.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; cool it within an hour of cooking and reheat in a hot skillet until steaming.
dinners.photo: A heaping plate of fried jasmine rice with browned diced steak, ribbons of scrambled egg and peas, carrots and corn.

dinners.title: Black pepper chicken
dinners.subtitle: Juicy grilled chicken with a bold cracked-pepper, garlic and soy glaze.

steps.text: Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Rub the chicken thighs with the oil and press the black pepper onto both sides. Grill the thighs, turning once halfway, until browned and a thermometer pushed into the thickest one reads 165°F: 10–14 minutes on an open grill, 6–8 minutes if yours closes like a press. Move to a clean plate, rest 5 minutes so the juices stay in, then slice across the grain.
While the chicken rests, simmer the soy sauce, honey and the 2 minced garlic cloves in a small saucepan over medium heat for 1 minute, until it smells garlicky and looks glossy.

steps: Toss the sliced chicken with the warm glaze and serve.
tips: Coarse-ground pepper gives the best crust. For kids who want it milder, pepper only half the thighs.
Get the potato wedges going first: they take the longest.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; slice it cold over a salad or reheat for wraps.
dinners.photo: Sliced grilled chicken with dark grill marks, coated in cracked black pepper and a shiny soy-garlic glaze, fanned on a plate.

dinners.title: Chicken & mushroom chow mein
dinners.subtitle: Noodles stir-fried with thin strips of chicken thigh, mushrooms, a whole bag of cabbage and ribbons of egg.

steps.text: Fill your largest pot with about 5 quarts of water, add 1 tablespoon of the salt, cover and bring to a full rolling boil over high heat. It takes 10–15 minutes, so start it first. While it heats, trim any big pieces of fat off the chicken thighs and slice them into thin strips. Whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar and sesame oil, mince the 3 garlic cloves and beat the 3 eggs.

Add the 12 oz of spaghetti (three-quarters of a 1 lb box) to the boiling water, stir for the first minute so it doesn’t stick, and boil uncovered until tender with a little bite, 8–10 minutes (check the box). Drain.
Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Spread half the oil on the griddle and sear the chicken in a single layer, turning, until browned and the thickest strips read 165°F, 5–7 minutes. Move it to a cooler part of the griddle.

Add the remaining oil and cook the mushrooms until browned, 4–5 minutes. Add the coleslaw mix and garlic and stir-fry until the cabbage softens, 2–3 minutes. Push aside and scramble the eggs until set.
Add the noodles and the sauce and toss everything together with the chicken until glossy and hot, about 2 minutes.

tips: Slice the chicken while it is still a little frozen; thin strips are much easier.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat in a skillet with a splash of water.
dinners.photo: Stir-fried noodles with seared strips of chicken, sliced mushrooms, shredded cabbage and strips of egg, piled on a platter.

dinners.title: Brown butter spaghetti with grilled chicken
dinners.subtitle: Spaghetti tossed in nutty brown butter, Parmesan and cracked pepper, topped with sliced grilled chicken.

steps.text: Fill your largest pot with about 5 quarts of water, add 1 tablespoon of the salt, cover and bring to a full rolling boil over high heat. It takes 10–15 minutes, so start it first.

Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Lay the chicken breasts between two sheets of plastic wrap (or in a zip bag) and pound the thick ends with a rolling pin or the bottom of a pan until each is an even ¾ inch thick, so they cook through without drying out. Rub them with the oil and season with the remaining 1 teaspoon of salt and half the pepper. Grill, turning once halfway, until marked and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F: 10–14 minutes on an open grill, 6–8 minutes if yours closes like a press. Move to a clean plate, rest 5 minutes so the juices stay in, then slice across the grain.

Add the 12 oz of spaghetti (three-quarters of a 1 lb box) to the boiling water, stir for the first minute so it doesn’t stick, and boil uncovered until tender with a little bite, 9–11 minutes (check the box). Scoop out 1 cup of the cooking water with a mug, then drain.

While the pasta cooks, melt the 5 tablespoons of butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Keep cooking, swirling the pan often, as it foams. In 4–6 minutes the foam settles, the bits on the bottom turn golden brown and it smells like toasted nuts. Pull the pan off the heat right then; it goes from brown to burnt quickly.

steps: Add the spaghetti, the Parmesan and the remaining pepper to the skillet with a splash of the saved water and toss with tongs until glossy, adding more water a little at a time. Divide among five plates and top with the sliced chicken.
tips: Use a light-colored pan if you have one so you can see the butter change color.
The pasta water is what makes it saucy: the starch in it helps the butter cling to the noodles.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat with a splash of water or milk so the sauce loosens.

dinners.title: Classic spaghetti with meat sauce
dinners.subtitle: Spaghetti under a hearty lean-beef marinara with grated carrot simmered in, and Parmesan on top.

Pour in the jar of Rao’s marinara and the can of diced tomatoes with its juice; the sauce is fully seasoned, so nothing else goes in. Turn the heat to medium-low and simmer gently, stirring now and then, for 10 minutes.

steps: Toss the spaghetti with about a third of the sauce, loosening with a splash of the saved water. Divide among five plates, spoon the rest of the sauce over the top and finish with the Parmesan.
tips: A sauce that looks dry needs pasta water, not more sauce.
dinners.leftovers: The meat sauce freezes for 3 months; make a double batch and freeze half flat in a zip bag.
dinners.photo: A generous plate of spaghetti topped with a thick, chunky tomato meat sauce and a snowfall of grated Parmesan.

dinners.title: Charred pepper & chicken sausage penne
dinners.subtitle: Ground chicken seasoned like Italian sausage and lots of blistered bell peppers in marinara with Parmesan.

Put the 2 lb of ground chicken in a large, deep skillet with the oil and sprinkle on the Italian seasoning, garlic powder, red pepper flakes and 1 teaspoon of the salt; that seasoning is what makes it taste like Italian sausage. tips: A dry, hot pan is what chars the peppers; oil just makes them steam.
Italian seasoning, garlic powder and a pinch of red pepper turn plain ground chicken into sausage; add a pinch of fennel seed if there is some in the cupboard.

dinners.subtitle: Grilled chicken over penne, marinara and a big bag of spinach under melted mozzarella and Parmesan.

dinners.subtitle: Grilled lemon-oregano chicken on warm naan with shredded romaine and a garlicky yogurt sauce.

Grill the thighs, turning once halfway, until browned and a thermometer pushed into the thickest one reads 165°F: 10–14 minutes on an open grill, 6–8 minutes if yours closes like a press. steps: Stir the remaining garlic and the juice of the second lemon into the yogurt. Shred the romaine heart.

steps.text: Warm the naan on the grill, about 1 minute per side, until soft with light grill marks.

steps: Top each naan with shredded romaine, sliced chicken and plenty of yogurt sauce, and fold to eat.
tips: Even 15 minutes in the lemon and oregano helps; you can also do it in the morning and leave it in the fridge.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; the chicken is good cold in a wrap with the yogurt sauce.

steps: Stir the 2 minced garlic cloves and the juice of the lemon into the yogurt with a splash of water until it drizzles.

tips: Start the potato wedges before the chicken; they take the longest.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; slice it cold over a salad.

dinners.subtitle: Barbecue-glazed grilled chicken piled with a tangy apple slaw on toasted buns.

steps: Core the apple and grate it on the large holes of a box grater. Toss it with the 10 oz of coleslaw mix, the yogurt, mustard and cider vinegar.

steps.text: Toss the sliced chicken with the remaining barbecue sauce. Toast the buns cut side down on the grill for about 1 minute.

steps: Fill the buns with the chicken and a tall pile of apple slaw.
tips: The slaw gets better as it sits; make it first.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; keep the chicken and slaw separate so the buns stay dry.
dinners.photo: A toasted bun piled high with sliced barbecue-glazed grilled chicken and crunchy apple coleslaw, on a plate.

dinners.title: Spiced beef flatbreads
dinners.subtitle: Grilled naan spread with hummus and topped with cumin-spiced lean beef, shredded romaine and a lemony yogurt drizzle.
steps: Peel the onion and chop it fine. Shred the romaine heart and stir the juice of the lemon into the yogurt.

Stir in the cumin, paprika, garlic powder, oregano, salt and ¼ cup of water and simmer until saucy, 2 minutes.
Warm the naan on the preheated electric grill, about 1 minute per side.

steps: Spread each naan with hummus, top with the spiced beef and shredded romaine and drizzle with the lemon yogurt. Cut into wedges.
tips: Toasting the spices in the hot beef for a minute before the water goes in makes them taste fuller.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; the spiced beef reheats well and makes a good rice bowl.
dinners.photo: Grilled naan flatbreads spread with creamy hummus and topped with cumin-spiced ground beef and shredded romaine, drizzled with yogurt and cut into wedges.

dinners.subtitle: Lemon-dressed romaine and carrots topped with grilled chicken breast and a scoop of hummus.

steps: Chop the 3 romaine hearts and shred the carrots. Whisk the juice of the 2 lemons with the remaining oil and salt and toss with the romaine and carrots in your biggest bowl.

tips: Dress the salad right before serving so the romaine stays crisp.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; keep the chicken separate from the dressed salad, which wilts overnight.
dinners.photo: A big bowl of chopped romaine and shredded carrots topped with sliced grilled chicken breast and a scoop of hummus dusted with paprika, lemon wedges alongside.

dinners.title: Seasoned beef tacos
dinners.subtitle: Taco-seasoned lean beef in warm street-taco corn tortillas with lettuce, cheddar and salsa.

steps.text: Set a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 2 lb of ground beef and break it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon as it cooks. Keep going until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 160°F, 8–10 minutes. Tip the pan and spoon off any liquid fat.
Stir in the two packets of La Preferida taco seasoning (they carry all the spices) with about 1 cup of water. Simmer, stirring now and then, until saucy rather than soupy, 3–5 minutes.

Warm the street-taco tortillas two or three at a time in a dry skillet over medium-high heat, 20–30 seconds per side, until soft with a few toasted spots. Stack them inside a clean kitchen towel so they stay warm and bendy.

steps: Shred the romaine heart and the cheddar. Fill three tortillas per person and pass the lettuce, cheese and salsa.
tips: Corn tortillas crack when they are cold; warm them right before eating and keep them wrapped in the towel.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container. The filling reheats well in a skillet; warm fresh tortillas to go with it.
dinners.photo: Three small street-taco corn tortillas filled with seasoned ground beef and topped with shredded lettuce, cheddar and salsa, on a plate.

dinners.title: Sizzling chicken fajitas
dinners.subtitle: Pre-seasoned fajita chicken seared with a big pile of charred peppers and onions, tucked into warm street-taco tortillas.
steps: Cut the 4 peppers and the onions into strips. Slice the chicken into strips if it isn’t already; Buena Mesa fajita chicken comes seasoned, so it needs nothing else.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Toss the peppers and onions with the oil on one side of the griddle and cook, turning now and then, until tender and charred at the edges, 8–10 minutes.
Sear the chicken on the other side in a single layer, turning, until browned and the thickest strips read 165°F, 6–8 minutes. Toss it with the vegetables.
Warm the tortillas on a clean part of the griddle, about 15 seconds per side. Serve three per person with the fajita filling and a spoonful of yogurt.

tips: Start the vegetables first; they take a couple of minutes longer than the chicken.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container. The filling reheats well in a skillet; warm fresh tortillas to go with it.
dinners.photo: Sizzling strips of seasoned chicken with charred red, green and yellow pepper strips and onions beside small warm flour tortillas and a dollop of white cream.

dinners.title: Chicken & black bean quesadillas
dinners.subtitle: Crispy griddled tortillas stuffed with fajita-sauced chicken, black beans and melted cheddar.
steps: Cut the chicken thighs into small ½-inch dice. Drain the can of black beans and mash them in a bowl with 4 tablespoons of the salsa.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.

Spread half the oil on the griddle and cook the chicken, turning, until browned and the thickest pieces read 165°F, 6–8 minutes. Scoop it into the bowl of beans, add the Cholula fajita sauce (it brings all the seasoning) and mix.
Turn the griddle down to medium and wipe on the remaining oil. Lay down the tortillas, spread the filling and the shredded cheddar over half of each and fold shut.
Toast until golden, 2–3 minutes per side, pressing gently with the spatula, until the cheese melts. Cut into wedges and serve with the remaining salsa and the yogurt.

tips: Keep the filling an inch from the edge so it doesn’t squeeze out when you press.
Medium heat matters: too hot and the tortilla browns before the cheese melts.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat in a dry skillet so they crisp back up.
dinners.photo: Golden crispy quesadilla wedges oozing melted cheddar, seasoned chicken and black beans, with salsa and a dollop of cream on the side.

dinners.title: Beef burrito bowls
dinners.subtitle: Basmati rice, lean taco beef, black beans and corn finished with romaine, salsa, cheddar and lime.

steps.text: Rinse the 1½ cups of basmati rice in a fine strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium saucepan with 2¼ cups of water and ½ teaspoon of the salt and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid, then take it off the heat and leave it covered 10 minutes more. Fluff with a fork. Squeeze in the juice of half the lime.

Set a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 2 lb of ground beef and break it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon as it cooks. Keep going until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 160°F, 8–10 minutes. Tip the pan and spoon off any liquid fat.
Stir in the taco seasoning, the rinsed and drained black beans and ½ cup of water and simmer 3 minutes.
Cook the 1 lb of frozen corn in a small saucepan with a splash of water until hot, 3–4 minutes, and drain.

steps: Shred the romaine heart and the cheddar. Build bowls with rice, beef and beans, corn and plenty of lettuce, and finish with salsa, cheese and the rest of the lime in wedges.
tips: Set the toppings out in bowls and let everyone build their own.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; pack rice, beef and beans together for lunch and add the lettuce fresh.
dinners.photo: A burrito bowl with basmati rice, taco-seasoned ground beef, black beans, corn, shredded lettuce, cheddar and salsa, with a lime wedge.

dinners.title: Beef & potato burritos
dinners.subtitle: Golden potato cubes, seasoned lean beef, peppers and cheddar rolled up and toasted seam side down.

steps.text: Scrub the 1½ lb of potatoes and cut into ½-inch cubes. Put them in a microwave-safe bowl with 2 tablespoons of water, cover with a plate and microwave, stirring halfway, until just tender, 6–8 minutes. Drain well.

Dice the 2 peppers and the onion. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the potatoes, peppers and onion with the salt, stirring only every couple of minutes, until golden and the onion is soft, 8–10 minutes. Move to a bowl.

Set the same skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 2 lb of ground beef and break it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon as it cooks. Keep going until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 160°F, 8–10 minutes. Tip the pan and spoon off any liquid fat.
Stir in the taco seasoning and ½ cup of water and simmer until saucy, about 2 minutes. Fold in the potatoes.

Fill each tortilla with the beef mixture, some shredded cheddar and a spoonful of salsa. Fold in the sides, roll snugly and toast seam side down in a dry skillet over medium heat until golden, 1–2 minutes per side. Two per person.

tips: Microwaving the potatoes first means they only need one spoon of oil to turn golden.
Warm the tortillas 10 seconds in the microwave so they roll without tearing.
dinners.leftovers: Wrap extra burritos in foil: they keep 3 days in the fridge or 2 months in the freezer, and reheat in a dry skillet.
dinners.photo: Two golden toasted flour tortilla burritos, one cut open to show seasoned ground beef, crispy potato cubes, peppers and melted cheese, with salsa on the side.

dinners.title: Chicken & street corn flatbreads
dinners.subtitle: Grilled chicken and creamy lime street corn over black-bean-smeared grilled naan.

steps.text: Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Season the chicken thighs with half the paprika and the salt. Warm the naan on the grill, about 1 minute per side. Spread with the beans, spoon over the street corn, top with the chicken and cut into wedges.

tips: Let the corn sit still in the pan between stirs; that is how it chars.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; keep the toppings separate and warm fresh naan.
dinners.photo: Grilled naan flatbreads topped with mashed black beans, creamy charred corn and sliced grilled chicken, dusted with paprika and cut into wedges with lime.

dinners.subtitle: Crispy air-fried personal cheese pizzas topped with Italian-seasoned grilled chicken breast.

steps.text: Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Lay the chicken breasts between two sheets of plastic wrap (or in a zip bag) and pound the thick ends with a rolling pin or the bottom of a pan until each is an even ¾ inch thick, so they cook through without drying out. Rub them with the oil and season with the Italian seasoning and salt. Grill, turning once halfway, until marked and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F: 10–14 minutes on an open grill, 6–8 minutes if yours closes like a press. Move to a clean plate, rest 5 minutes so the juices stay in, then slice thin.

steps: Use personal cheese pizzas that fit flat in your air fryer and have air-fryer directions on the box. Keep them frozen until you cook them.

steps.text: Air-fry one or two pizzas at a time at the temperature and time on the box (usually about 380°F for 6–8 minutes). Scatter sliced chicken over each pizza for the last 2 minutes so it heats through.
Let each pizza stand 1–2 minutes so the cheese sets, then cut and serve.

tips: Start the salad and carrot sticks while the pizzas take their turns in the air fryer.
Keep finished pizzas warm under a loose tent of foil.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat slices in the air fryer at 350°F for 3 minutes.
dinners.photo: A crispy personal cheese pizza with bubbly golden mozzarella topped with strips of grilled chicken, cut into wedges on a board.

dinners.title: Chili-stuffed potatoes
dinners.subtitle: Fluffy split potatoes piled with chicken chili, melted cheddar and a cool dollop of yogurt.

steps.text: Scrub the 3 lb of potatoes (5 medium) and poke each one 5 or 6 times with a fork. Microwave on a plate, three at a time, turning them over halfway, until a knife slides into the center with no resistance: 8–10 minutes for three, a few minutes more for big ones. Careful, they’re steaming hot.

Set a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat; lean ground chicken browns fine without oil in a nonstick pan. Add the 2 lb of ground chicken and the salt and break it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon as it cooks. Keep going until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 165°F, 8–10 minutes.
Stir in the 2 cans of Bush’s chili beans with their sauce (it is already chili-seasoned, so no spices are needed) and simmer, stirring now and then, until thick, 8–10 minutes.

steps: Split the potatoes, fluff the insides with a fork, spoon on the chili and finish with shredded cheddar and a spoonful of yogurt.
tips: Start the chili while the first batch of potatoes is in the microwave.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge in a covered container; the chili freezes for 3 months.
dinners.photo: Fluffy split golden potatoes heaped with chunky chicken and bean chili, melted cheddar and a dollop of white yogurt.

dinners.title: Chicken sausage, egg & potato breakfast tacos
dinners.subtitle: Breakfast-for-dinner tacos with homemade lean chicken sausage, soft scrambled eggs, golden potatoes, peppers and cheddar.

steps.text: Scrub the 1½ lb of potatoes and cut into ½-inch cubes. Put them in a microwave-safe bowl with 2 tablespoons of water, cover with a plate and microwave, stirring halfway, until just tender, 6–8 minutes. Drain. Dice the 2 peppers and beat the 10 eggs in a bowl.
Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.

Put the 1½ lb of ground chicken on the griddle and sprinkle it with the Italian seasoning, garlic powder, paprika, black pepper and ½ teaspoon of the salt; that seasoning turns it into breakfast sausage. Cook, breaking it up, until no pink is left and it reads 165°F, 8–10 minutes. Move it to a cooler part.
Spread the oil on the hot part and cook the potatoes and peppers with the rest of the salt until golden, 6–8 minutes.
Turn the griddle down to medium, pour the eggs onto a clean part and gently push them around with a spatula until just set, 1–2 minutes. Fold in the sausage, potatoes and shredded cheddar.

steps: Warm the street-taco tortillas on the griddle and fill three per person, with salsa on top.
tips: Take the eggs off while they still look a little glossy; they finish cooking from their own heat.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; roll the filling in a tortilla and microwave 45 seconds for tomorrow’s breakfast.
dinners.photo: Soft flour tortilla tacos filled with fluffy scrambled eggs, crumbled chicken sausage, golden potato cubes, peppers and melted cheddar, topped with salsa.

dinners.title: Chicken cheddar melts
dinners.subtitle: Golden skillet-toasted sandwiches packed with sliced grilled chicken and melted cheese.

steps.text: Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Season the chicken thighs with the garlic powder and salt. Grill the thighs, turning once halfway, until browned and a thermometer pushed into the thickest one reads 165°F: 10–14 minutes on an open grill, 6–8 minutes if yours closes like a press. Move to a clean plate, rest 5 minutes so the juices stay in, then slice thin.

steps: Spread a thin layer of the butter on one side of each of the 10 bread slices. Build five sandwiches with the buttered sides out: a cheese slice and a generous layer of chicken in each.

steps.text: Toast in a large skillet over medium-low heat, two at a time, until deep golden and the cheese has melted, 3–4 minutes per side. Cut in half.

tips: Medium-low heat gives the cheese time to melt before the bread gets too dark.
Put the tomato soup on to simmer before you start toasting.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; store the chicken on its own and build fresh sandwiches.
dinners.photo: Golden buttery grilled cheese sandwiches stuffed with sliced chicken and melted cheese, cut diagonally and stacked to show the gooey center.

dinners.title: Sweet & tangy sloppy joes
dinners.subtitle: Sweet-tangy lean beef simmered with peppers and onions, piled high on toasted buns.
steps: Finely dice the onion and the 2 peppers.

steps.text: Set a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 2 lb of ground beef, the onion and the peppers and break it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon as it cooks. Keep going until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 160°F, 8–10 minutes. The onion and peppers cook soft along with the meat. Tip the pan and spoon off any liquid fat.
Stir in the can of diced tomatoes with its juice, the ketchup, brown sugar, mustard, cider vinegar and salt. Simmer, stirring now and then, until thick enough to pile on a bun, 8–10 minutes.
Toast the buns cut side down in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 1 minute, then pile them high with the beef.

tips: If it still looks runny, simmer a few minutes more; it thickens fast at the end.
dinners.leftovers: The meat keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; it is a good one to double.
dinners.photo: A toasted bun overflowing with saucy sweet-and-tangy sloppy joe beef with soft cooked peppers and onions, on a plate.

dinners.title: Crispy Parmesan chicken fingers
dinners.subtitle: Panko-Parmesan crusted chicken strips from the air fryer with a honey-mustard dip.
steps: Cut the chicken breasts into finger-size strips and season with the salt and garlic powder.

Set up three shallow dishes: the flour, the 2 beaten eggs, and the panko mixed with the Parmesan and rubbed with the oil until it feels like damp sand. Coat each strip in flour, dip in egg, then press into the crumbs. Throw away any coating left over; it touched raw chicken.

steps.text: Heat the air fryer to 390°F. Cook the strips in single layers, turning halfway, until golden and a thermometer in the thickest strip reads 165°F, 10–14 minutes per batch.

steps: Stir the yogurt, mustard and honey into a dip and serve with the chicken.
tips: Use one hand for the dry dishes and the other for the egg so your fingers don’t get breaded.
Leave space between the strips; crowded strips come out pale and soft.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat in the air fryer at 370°F for 4 minutes to bring the crunch back.
dinners.photo: Golden crispy panko-crusted chicken tenders stacked on a plate with a small bowl of creamy honey-mustard dip.

dinners.title: Chicken, broccoli & cheddar potatoes
dinners.subtitle: Fluffy split potatoes loaded with grilled chicken, broccoli and melted cheddar.

steps.text: Scrub the 3 lb of potatoes (5 medium) and poke each one 5 or 6 times with a fork. Microwave on a plate, three at a time, turning them over halfway, until a knife slides into the center with no resistance: 8–10 minutes for three, a few minutes more for big ones. Careful, they’re steaming hot.

Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Lay the chicken breasts between two sheets of plastic wrap (or in a zip bag) and pound the thick ends with a rolling pin or the bottom of a pan until each is an even ¾ inch thick, so they cook through without drying out. Season them with half the salt and the pepper. Grill, turning once halfway, until marked and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F: 10–14 minutes on an open grill, 6–8 minutes if yours closes like a press. Move to a clean plate, rest 5 minutes so the juices stay in, then cut into bite-size pieces.
Steam the 1½ lb of frozen broccoli in a covered saucepan with ½ inch of boiling water until tender, 5–7 minutes, and drain well.
Split the potatoes and fluff the insides with the butter, yogurt and remaining salt. Top with broccoli, chicken and shredded cheddar, then microwave 30–60 seconds to melt the cheese.

tips: Grill the chicken while the potatoes are in the microwave and everything is ready together.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat a loaded potato in the microwave for 2 minutes.
dinners.photo: Split fluffy golden potatoes loaded with steamed broccoli florets, diced grilled chicken and gooey melted cheddar.

dinners.title: BBQ pulled pork sandwiches
dinners.subtitle: Smoky barbecue pulled pork warmed through and piled on toasted buns with dill pickles.
steps: Empty about 2½ lb of the pulled pork into a large saucepan (most of the 3 lb tray; the rest makes a good lunch). It comes sauced and seasoned (Jack Daniel’s), so nothing else goes in.

steps.text: Cover and warm over medium-low heat, stirring every few minutes, until steaming and a thermometer in the middle reads 165°F, 10–12 minutes. Add a splash of water if it gets thick.
Toast the buns cut side down in a dry skillet over medium heat, about 1 minute.

steps: Pile the pork on the buns and top with pickles. Six sandwiches: one each, and one to split. A spoonful of the lime slaw on top is good too.
tips: Start the fries first; the pork only needs 10 minutes.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat with a splash of water.
dinners.photo: A toasted bun piled high with saucy shredded barbecue pulled pork and dill pickles, with french fries and creamy coleslaw on the plate.

dinners.title: Smoked sausage, chicken & Cajun potato skillet
dinners.subtitle: Smoked sausage coins and diced chicken with lots of peppers, onion and Cajun-seasoned potatoes in one big skillet.
steps: Slice one rope of smoked sausage into ½-inch coins and cut the chicken breast into ¾-inch pieces. Cut the 2 peppers and the onion into strips. Drain the 3 cans of potatoes well.

steps.text: Heat the oil in your largest skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, sprinkle with the Slap Ya Mama Cajun seasoning and cook, stirring, until browned and the thickest pieces read 165°F, 6–8 minutes. Add the sausage for the last 3 minutes to brown, then push everything to one side.
Add the peppers and onion strips and cook until softened and browned at the edges, about 5 minutes.

Add the Del Monte Cajun-style potatoes (they are already seasoned, so no more spice or salt is needed) and cook, stirring now and then, until golden in spots and everything is steaming hot, at least 165°F, 6–8 minutes.

tips: Pat the canned potatoes dry so they brown instead of steaming.
One rope of sausage is plenty for flavor; the chicken does the rest.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat in a skillet, and try it with a fried egg on top.
dinners.photo: A big skillet of browned smoked sausage coins and diced chicken with golden potatoes and strips of red and green bell pepper and cooked onion, flecked with Cajun spice.

dinners.title: Chicken Alfredo night
dinners.subtitle: Heat-and-serve chicken Alfredo stretched with a pound of broccoli, with garlic toast and a crisp salad.
steps: Spoon the chicken Alfredo from its tray into a large, deep skillet and add the milk. It comes fully seasoned from the Member’s Mark deli, so nothing else goes in.

steps.text: Cover and warm over medium-low heat, stirring gently every few minutes, until it is hot all the way through and a thermometer in the middle reads 165°F, 10–12 minutes. Add another splash of milk if the sauce tightens.
While it warms, put the 1 lb of frozen broccoli in a microwave-safe bowl with 2 tablespoons of water, cover with a plate and microwave until hot and bright green, 4–5 minutes. Drain it well.

steps: Fold the broccoli into the Alfredo and divide among five plates.
tips: Stir from the bottom so the sauce doesn’t catch.
Drain the broccoli well, or it thins the sauce.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat gently with a splash of milk.
dinners.photo: A plate of creamy fettuccine chicken Alfredo with tender chicken pieces and bright green broccoli florets in a glossy white sauce, topped with cracked black pepper.

dinners.title: BBQ chicken naan pizzas
dinners.subtitle: Warm naan topped with barbecue pulled chicken and melted mozzarella, crisped on the griddle.
steps: Toss the 1½ lb of pulled chicken with 2 tablespoons of the barbecue sauce; it comes seasoned, so it needs nothing else.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-low for 5 minutes.

steps: Spread the remaining barbecue sauce thinly over the 5 naan, then top with the chicken and the mozzarella.

steps.text: Set the naan on the griddle, cover with a dome or a loose sheet of foil and cook until the bottoms are crisp, the cheese has melted and the chicken reads 165°F, 4–6 minutes. Cut into wedges.

tips: Low heat and a cover are what melt the cheese before the bottom scorches.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat wedges in the air fryer at 350°F for 3 minutes.
dinners.photo: Golden naan flatbread pizzas topped with barbecue pulled chicken and bubbly melted mozzarella, cut into wedges on a board.

dinners.title: Teriyaki chicken & noodles
dinners.subtitle: Seared chicken and a big bag of stir-fry vegetables tossed with sweet-savory teriyaki noodles.
steps: Cut the chicken breasts into 1-inch pieces and season with the salt.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large, wide pot over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Cook the chicken in two batches, stirring, until browned and the thickest pieces read 165°F, 6–8 minutes per batch. Move it to a plate.

In the same pot bring the water the three noodle pouches call for (about 2 cups per pouch) and the butter to a boil. Stir in all three Knorr teriyaki pouches and the 1½ lb of frozen vegetables; the seasoning in the pouch makes the whole sauce, so nothing else goes in.
Turn the heat to medium and simmer, stirring now and then, until the noodles are tender and the sauce has thickened, about 8 minutes. Fold the chicken back in and serve.

tips: The sauce thickens as it stands; if it gets tight, loosen it with a splash of water.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat with a splash of water.
dinners.photo: A bowl of glossy teriyaki noodles tossed with seared chicken pieces, broccoli, carrots and peas.

dinners.title: Teriyaki chicken rice bowls
dinners.subtitle: Grilled chicken thighs lacquered in homemade garlic-ginger teriyaki over jasmine rice.

steps.text: Rinse the 1½ cups of jasmine rice in a fine strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium saucepan with 2¼ cups of water and ½ teaspoon of the salt and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid, then take it off the heat and leave it covered 10 minutes more. Fluff with a fork.

Make the teriyaki: in a small saucepan whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar, honey, rice vinegar, the 3 minced garlic cloves, the grated ginger, the cornstarch and ½ cup of water. Simmer over medium heat, stirring, until thick and glossy, 2–3 minutes. Pour a third of it into a separate cup for brushing.

Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Grill the chicken thighs plain, and brush them with the cup of teriyaki during the last 2 minutes so it turns sticky without burning. Grill the thighs, turning once halfway, until browned and a thermometer pushed into the thickest one reads 165°F: 10–14 minutes on an open grill, 6–8 minutes if yours closes like a press. Move to a clean plate, rest 5 minutes so the juices stay in, then slice across the grain.

steps: Serve the sliced chicken over the rice with the rest of the sauce from the pan and a drizzle of the sesame oil.
tips: Keep the brushing sauce separate from the serving sauce, since the brush touches raw chicken.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; pack chicken and rice together for an easy lunch bowl.
dinners.photo: Sliced grilled chicken thighs glazed in glossy dark teriyaki sauce over a mound of white jasmine rice, extra sauce drizzled on top.

dinners.title: Egg roll in a bowl
dinners.subtitle: All the flavor of an egg roll (lean ground chicken, a bag and a half of cabbage, carrots, ginger and garlic) in one big skillet.
steps: Shred the carrots, mince the 4 garlic cloves and grate the ginger.

steps.text: Heat the oil in your largest skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 2.25 lb of ground chicken and break it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon as it cooks. Keep going until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 165°F, 8–10 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then add the coleslaw mix (a bag and a half) and the carrots in two additions, tossing until the cabbage wilts but keeps some crunch, 4–5 minutes.

steps: Stir in the soy sauce and rice vinegar, drizzle with the sesame oil and serve in bowls.
tips: The cabbage looks like too much at first; it cooks down by half in a couple of minutes.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; it reheats well in the microwave and makes a good lunch.
dinners.photo: A bowl of savory stir-fried ground chicken with wilted shredded cabbage and carrots, glistening with soy and sesame oil.

dinners.title: Korean-style beef bowls
dinners.subtitle: Sweet-savory garlic, ginger and sesame lean ground beef over jasmine rice with a pile of crunchy carrots.

steps.text: Rinse the 1½ cups of jasmine rice in a fine strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium saucepan with 2¼ cups of water and ½ teaspoon of the salt and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid, then take it off the heat and leave it covered 10 minutes more. Fluff with a fork.

steps: Whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, rice vinegar and red pepper flakes (skip them for no heat). Shred the 1 lb of carrots, mince the 4 garlic cloves and grate the ginger.

steps.text: Set a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 2 lb of ground beef and break it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon as it cooks. Keep going until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 160°F, 8–10 minutes. Tip the pan and spoon off any liquid fat.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then pour in the sauce and simmer until the beef is glazed and sticky, 2–3 minutes.

steps: Spoon the beef over the rice and top each bowl with a big handful of the shredded carrots.
tips: Break the beef into very small crumbles; more edges means more glaze.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; it is just as good cold in a lettuce wrap.
dinners.photo: A bowl of white jasmine rice topped with glossy caramelized Korean-style ground beef and shredded carrots, drizzled with sesame oil.

dinners.title: Chicken sausage & broccoli penne
dinners.subtitle: Ground chicken seasoned like Italian sausage, lots of garlicky broccoli and penne tossed with Parmesan, lemon and a splash of broth.

steps.text: Fill your largest pot with about 5 quarts of water, add 1 tablespoon of the salt, cover and bring to a full rolling boil over high heat. It takes 10–15 minutes, so start it first. Mince the 4 garlic cloves.

Add the 12 oz of penne (three-quarters of a 1 lb box) to the boiling water, stir for the first minute so it doesn’t stick, and boil uncovered until tender with a little bite, 10–12 minutes (check the box). Add the 1¾ lb of frozen broccoli to the pot for the last 2 minutes. Scoop out 1 cup of the cooking water with a mug, then drain.

Put the 2 lb of ground chicken in a large, deep skillet with the oil and sprinkle on the Italian seasoning, garlic powder and 1 teaspoon of the salt; that seasoning is what makes it taste like Italian sausage. Cook over medium-high heat, breaking it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon, until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 165°F, 8–10 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and red pepper flakes for 30 seconds, then pour in the cup of chicken stock and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan.

steps: Add the penne and broccoli, the Parmesan and the juice of the lemon, and toss with splashes of the saved water until glossy.
tips: The browned bits on the bottom of the pan are flavor; the stock lifts them into the sauce.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat with a splash of water or milk so the sauce loosens.
dinners.photo: Penne tossed with browned crumbled chicken sausage, bright green broccoli florets, garlic and grated Parmesan in a wide pasta bowl.

dinners.title: Chicken Cobb salad
dinners.subtitle: A big chopped salad with grilled chicken breast, bacon, hard-cooked egg and cheddar with ranch.

steps.text: Put the 5 eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water by an inch and bring to a boil. Cover, turn off the heat and let stand 11 minutes, then cool in ice water, peel and quarter.

Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Lay the chicken breasts between two sheets of plastic wrap (or in a zip bag) and pound the thick ends with a rolling pin or the bottom of a pan until each is an even ¾ inch thick, so they cook through without drying out. Rub them with the oil, salt and pepper. Grill, turning once halfway, until marked and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F: 10–14 minutes on an open grill, 6–8 minutes if yours closes like a press. Move to a clean plate, rest 5 minutes so the juices stay in, then slice across the grain.
Warm the 5 slices of fully cooked bacon in a dry skillet over medium heat until crisp, about 1 minute per side, and crumble.

steps: Chop the 3 romaine hearts and divide among five big bowls. Arrange rows of chicken, bacon, egg and shredded cheddar on top and serve with the ranch.
tips: Older eggs peel more easily than fresh ones.
Serve the ranch on the side so everyone dresses their own.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; store the toppings separately from the lettuce.
dinners.photo: A large bowl of chopped romaine with neat rows of sliced grilled chicken, crumbled bacon, quartered hard-cooked eggs and shredded cheddar, ranch on the side.

dinners.title: Chicken taco salad
dinners.subtitle: Crisp romaine loaded with taco-spiced ground chicken, black beans, cheddar, salsa, a cool yogurt topping and a few crunchy chips.

steps.text: Set a large skillet over medium-high heat; lean ground chicken browns fine without oil in a nonstick pan. Add the 2 lb of ground chicken and break it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon as it cooks. Keep going until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 165°F, 8–10 minutes.
Stir in the taco seasoning, the rinsed and drained black beans and ½ cup of water and simmer until saucy, 3–4 minutes.

steps: Chop the 3 romaine hearts and divide among five big bowls. Top with the warm chicken, shredded cheddar, salsa and a spoonful of yogurt.
Crush a small handful of chips over each salad and finish with a squeeze of lime.
tips: Plain Greek yogurt does the job of sour cream here.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat the taco meat and build a fresh salad for lunch.
dinners.photo: A big taco salad of chopped romaine topped with seasoned ground chicken, black beans, shredded cheddar, salsa, a dollop of yogurt and crushed tortilla chips, with a lime wedge.

dinners.title: Sesame-ginger chicken salad
dinners.subtitle: Grilled chicken breast over romaine and crunchy cabbage with fresh orange and a sesame-ginger dressing.

steps.text: Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Lay the chicken breasts between two sheets of plastic wrap (or in a zip bag) and pound the thick ends with a rolling pin or the bottom of a pan until each is an even ¾ inch thick, so they cook through without drying out. Rub them with 1 tablespoon of the oil and 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce. Grill, turning once halfway, until marked and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F: 10–14 minutes on an open grill, 6–8 minutes if yours closes like a press. Move to a clean plate, rest 5 minutes so the juices stay in, then slice across the grain.

steps: Whisk the remaining soy sauce and oil with the rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey, grated ginger and the grated garlic clove.
Chop the 2 romaine hearts, shred the carrots and peel and segment the oranges. Toss the romaine, coleslaw mix and carrots with most of the dressing.
Divide among five bowls, top with the chicken and orange segments and drizzle with the rest of the dressing.
tips: Dress the salad right before serving so it stays crunchy.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; keep the chicken and dressing separate from the greens.
dinners.photo: A colorful salad of romaine and shredded cabbage with carrots and orange segments topped with sliced grilled chicken and a glossy sesame-ginger dressing.

dinners.title: Chicken & bean chili
dinners.subtitle: A big pot of hearty chicken chili with beans, tomatoes and peppers, topped with cheddar and a spoonful of yogurt.

steps.text: Dice the onion and the pepper. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and cook them, stirring, until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the 2 lb of ground chicken and break it into small crumbles as it cooks, until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 165°F, 8–10 minutes.

steps: Stir in the packet of taco seasoning, the 2 cans of Bush’s chili beans with their sauce and the 2 cans of diced tomatoes with their juice. Between the packet and the beans the pot is fully seasoned.

steps.text: Bring to a boil, then turn the heat to low and simmer, partly covered and stirring now and then, until thick, 15–20 minutes. Ladle into bowls and top with shredded cheddar and a spoonful of yogurt.

tips: This is a good one for the PossibleCooker: brown the chicken on SEAR/SAUTÉ, add everything else and SLOW COOK on LO for 6 hours.
Chili is better the next day.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; freeze it flat in zip bags so it thaws quickly.
dinners.photo: A deep bowl of thick chicken and bean chili with tomatoes and peppers, topped with shredded cheddar and a dollop of yogurt.

dinners.title: Beef stroganoff noodles
dinners.subtitle: Lean ground beef and a pound of mushrooms in a creamy gravy over egg noodles.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with 2 teaspoons of the salt. Cook the 12 oz of egg noodles until tender, 6–8 minutes, drain and toss with the butter.

steps: Peel the onion and cut it into small dice. Mince the 3 garlic cloves.

steps.text: Set a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 2 lb of ground beef, the onion and the 16 oz of mushrooms and break it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon as it cooks. Keep going until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 160°F, 8–10 minutes. Keep cooking until the mushrooms are browned and their liquid has cooked off, 2–4 minutes more. Tip the pan and spoon off any liquid fat.
Stir in the garlic, flour, paprika, pepper and the remaining 1 teaspoon of salt and cook 1 minute. Pour in the 2 cups of chicken stock and simmer, stirring, until thickened to a gravy, 3–4 minutes.

steps: Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sour cream and yogurt until creamy. Spoon over the noodles.
tips: Off the heat is important for the sour cream and yogurt: boiling splits them.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container. Reheat gently; boiling splits the sauce.
dinners.photo: Wide egg noodles topped with a creamy beef and mushroom stroganoff sauce, sprinkled with black pepper.

dinners.title: Bacon cheeseburger smashburgers
dinners.subtitle: Double smashed patties with a strip of crispy bacon, melted cheese, lettuce and a tangy burger sauce.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two. While it heats, stir the mayo, yogurt and ketchup with 1 tablespoon of finely chopped pickles for the burger sauce. Shred the romaine heart and divide the 2 lb of beef into 10 loose balls, a little over 3 oz each.
Crisp the 5 slices of fully cooked bacon on the griddle, about 30 seconds per side, and set them on a paper towel.

Set 5 balls on the griddle, smash each one flat and thin with a sturdy spatula and season with a pinch of the salt and pepper. Cook until the edges are deep brown and crisp, 2–3 minutes, then scrape, flip and lay a cheese slice on every other patty.
Cook 1–2 minutes more, until a thermometer slid in from the side reads 160°F. Repeat with the other 5 balls, then toast the buns cut side down on a clean part of the griddle.

steps: Spread the buns with the burger sauce and stack two patties on each with a strip of bacon, the rest of the pickles and shredded lettuce.
tips: One strip of bacon broken in half covers the whole bun.
Cold beef smashes best: keep the balls in the fridge until the griddle is hot.
dinners.leftovers: Cooked patties keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat in a covered skillet with a splash of water for 2–3 minutes.
dinners.photo: A double smashburger with a crispy bacon strip, melted cheddar, pickles, shredded lettuce and burger sauce on a toasted bun, plated with french fries.

dinners.title: Chicken Philly cheesesteaks
dinners.subtitle: Thin-sliced griddled chicken breast with lots of peppers and onions and melted cheese in toasted hoagie rolls.
steps: Slice the chicken breasts as thin as you can (it is easier if they are still partly frozen). Season with the garlic powder, salt and pepper. Cut the 3 peppers and the onions into thin strips.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Spread the oil on the griddle and cook the peppers and onions on one side until soft and browned, 8–10 minutes.
Cook the chicken on the other side in a thin layer, chopping and turning it with two spatulas, until no pink is left and the thickest pieces read 165°F, 5–7 minutes.
Mix the chicken and vegetables into five piles, top with the mozzarella and cover for 1 minute to melt. Spread the rolls thinly with the mayo, toast them on the griddle and scoop a pile into each.

tips: Twenty minutes in the freezer firms the chicken up enough to shave it thin.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat the filling in a skillet and toast a fresh roll.
dinners.photo: A toasted hoagie roll overflowing with thin-sliced griddled chicken, sautéed peppers and onions and gooey melted cheese.

dinners.title: Blackened Cajun chicken
dinners.subtitle: Slap Ya Mama–rubbed chicken breasts seared hard on the Blackstone and finished with a little Kerrygold.
steps: Lay the chicken breasts between two sheets of plastic wrap (or in a zip bag) and pound the thick ends with a rolling pin or the bottom of a pan until each is an even ¾ inch thick, so they cook through without drying out. Pat them dry and rub with the oil.
Season all over with the Slap Ya Mama Cajun seasoning and the smoked paprika. It is salty, so don’t add salt.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Lay the chicken on the griddle and leave it alone 5–6 minutes, until a dark, spicy crust forms and it lets go of the griddle easily.
Flip and cook 4–6 minutes more, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F. Top each piece with a small dab of the butter as it comes off, rest 5 minutes and slice.

tips: Blackened means a dark spice crust, not burnt: if it smokes hard, turn the heat down a notch.
Go lighter on the seasoning for anyone who doesn’t love heat.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; slice it for wraps or over a salad.
dinners.photo: Sliced blackened Cajun chicken breasts with a dark spice crust and melting butter on a plate beside golden Cajun diced potatoes and buttered corn.

dinners.title: Mango habanero chicken thighs
dinners.subtitle: Rubbed with Badia mango pepper, grilled, then glazed with Buffalo Wild Wings mango habanero sauce.
steps: Pat the chicken thighs dry, toss with the oil, then season both sides with the Badia mango pepper seasoning and the salt.

steps.text: Heat the electric grill (or the outdoor grill) to medium-high for 5 minutes. Grill the chicken 5–6 minutes per side, until a thermometer in the thickest thigh reads 165°F.
Brush the mango habanero sauce over both sides for the last 2 minutes, turning once, so it turns sticky without burning.

steps: Rest 5 minutes and drizzle any sauce left in the bowl over the top. It is sweet with real heat, so go light on the glaze for anyone who wants it milder.
tips: Glaze two or three thighs lightly, or not at all, for the kids.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; chop it into a rice bowl or a wrap.
dinners.photo: Grilled chicken thighs with char marks and a glossy orange mango habanero glaze, served with golden turmeric rice and steamed broccoli.

dinners.title: Chicago-style Italian beef
dinners.subtitle: Shaved roast beef soaked in a seasoned jus, piled on rolls and topped with Buona hot giardiniera.

steps.text: In a wide pot, simmer the 3 cups of chicken stock with the Italian seasoning, garlic powder, oregano, crushed red pepper and black pepper over medium heat for 5 minutes. This is the jus.
Turn the heat to low and add the shaved roast beef, pulling the slices apart. Let it soak in the hot jus until steaming and 165°F, 3–4 minutes. Don’t let it boil or the beef toughens.

steps: Split the rolls without cutting all the way through. Pile the beef in with tongs and spoon jus over each one, or dip the whole sandwich, Chicago-style.
Top with the Buona hot giardiniera and serve extra jus on the side for dipping.
tips: Giardiniera is hot: serve it on the side and let everyone add their own.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; store the beef in its jus and rewarm gently without boiling.
dinners.photo: A Chicago-style Italian beef sandwich on a long roll, juicy shaved beef topped with colorful hot giardiniera, beside fries and grilled peppers.

dinners.title: Buffalo chicken ranch wraps
