dinners.subtitle: Griddled chicken tossed in Crystal hot sauce with a little butter, wrapped with lots of romaine, cheddar and Wish-Bone ranch.
steps: Cut the chicken breasts into thin strips and toss with the oil, garlic powder and salt. Chop the 2 romaine hearts.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Cook the strips in a single layer, 3–4 minutes per side, until browned and a thermometer in the thickest strip reads 165°F.
Meanwhile melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat and whisk in the Crystal hot sauce. Toss the cooked chicken in the sauce.

steps: Warm the tortillas on the griddle for 20 seconds a side. Fill each with a big handful of romaine, buffalo chicken and shredded cheddar, drizzle with the ranch and roll up tight. Two wraps per person.
tips: Toss only part of the chicken in the hot sauce if someone wants theirs plain.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; keep the chicken separate and roll fresh wraps for lunch.
dinners.photo: Two buffalo chicken wraps cut in half showing spicy orange chicken, crisp romaine, cheddar and ranch, with carrot sticks and a cup of ranch.

dinners.title: Cajun butter steak bites
dinners.subtitle: Lean eye of round cut into bites, seared hot and fast on the Blackstone with Slap Ya Mama and a little Kerrygold.
steps: Pat the eye of round steaks dry, trim off any silvery skin and cut the meat into 1-inch cubes.
Toss the cubes with the oil, soy sauce and Slap Ya Mama Cajun seasoning. It is salty, so don’t add salt.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on high for 10 minutes; this cut wants a very hot griddle.
Spread the steak in one layer (two batches if it is crowded) and sear without moving for 2 minutes, then turn and cook 1–2 minutes more, until a thermometer in a thick piece reads 145°F.
Push the steak together, drop the butter and black pepper on top and toss as it melts. Rest 3 minutes before serving.

tips: Eye of round is very lean, so cook it hot and fast and stop at medium; past that it turns tough.
Dry meat sears, wet meat steams: pat it well.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; slice the bites thin for steak sandwiches.
dinners.photo: Seared, glossy Cajun butter steak bites with a dark spice crust piled on a plate beside an ear of buttered corn on the cob and creamy potatoes.

dinners.title: Chorizo & nopalitos street tacos
dinners.subtitle: Lean ground beef with a little pork chorizo for flavor and tender jarred nopalitos, in Mission street taco tortillas.
steps: Drain the nopalitos in a strainer and rinse well under cold water to wash off the slippery brine, then pat dry.

steps.text: Squeeze the ½ lb of chorizo out of its casings into your largest skillet with the 1½ lb of ground beef. Cook over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 160°F, 8–10 minutes. Tip the pan and spoon off the red grease. Chorizo is fully seasoned, so nothing else goes in.
Stir in the nopalitos and cook 3–4 minutes more, until hot and catching a little color at the edges.
Warm the tortillas on the Blackstone or in a dry skillet for 20 seconds a side. Fill three per person with the chorizo and nopalitos, shredded cheese and salsa.

tips: Chorizo gives off a lot of fat; spooning it off is the difference between rich and greasy.
Out of tortillas? Spoon the filling over rice as a bowl.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container. The filling reheats well in a skillet; warm fresh tortillas to go with it.
dinners.photo: Small flour street tacos filled with crumbly red chorizo, ground beef and diced green nopalitos, topped with shredded cheese and salsa, with charro beans alongside.

dinners.title: Smoky beef & bean chili
dinners.subtitle: Lean ground beef with chili beans and fire-roasted tomatoes, seasoned with smoked paprika and Slap Ya Mama.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the 2 lb of ground beef and break it into small crumbles as it cooks, until no pink is left and a thermometer in the meat reads 160°F, 8–10 minutes.

steps: Stir in the smoked paprika and Slap Ya Mama Cajun seasoning for 30 seconds, then add the 2 cans of chili beans with their sauce and the can of diced tomatoes with its juice. The Serious Bean chipotle pintos on your shelf work as the chili beans, and a can of National Coney Island chili can go in too.

steps.text: Bring to a boil, then turn the heat to low and simmer, partly covered and stirring now and then, until thick, 15–20 minutes.

steps: Taste, then serve in bowls topped with shredded cheddar.
tips: Chili is better the next day.
It works in the PossibleCooker too: brown the beef on SEAR/SAUTÉ, add everything else and SLOW COOK on LO for 6 hours.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; freeze it flat in zip bags so it thaws quickly.
dinners.photo: A bowl of thick beef and bean chili topped with melting shredded cheddar, with buttered corn on the side.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker chicken tortilla soup
dinners.subtitle: Shredded chicken, black beans, corn and tomatoes in a mild taco-spiced broth, with cheddar, a few crushed chips and lime.
steps: Peel the onion and cut it into small dice; it cooks soft in the soup. Mince the 3 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse the 2 cans of black beans.

Put the onion, garlic, beans, the 1 lb of frozen corn, the 2 cans of diced tomatoes with their juice, the 6 cups of chicken stock, the salsa and the packet of taco seasoning in the PossibleCooker pot and stir. Lay the 2 lb of thawed chicken breasts on top and push them under the liquid.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out.

steps: Lift the chicken onto a plate. A thermometer in the thickest piece should read at least 165°F and the meat should pull apart easily. Shred it with two forks and stir it back into the soup.
Ladle into bowls and top each with shredded cheddar, a small handful of crushed tortilla chips and a squeeze of lime.
tips: Use thawed meat in the slow cooker, never frozen, so it heats through safely.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: The soup (without the chips) keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; cool it first and freeze flat in zip bags.
dinners.photo: A wide bowl of brothy chicken tortilla soup with shredded chicken, black beans, corn and cooked tomatoes, topped with shredded cheddar, crushed tortilla chips and a lime wedge.

dinners.title: White chicken chili
dinners.subtitle: Creamy, mild chili with shredded chicken, white beans, corn and green chiles, finished with Greek yogurt and lime.
steps: Peel the onion and cut it into small dice; it cooks soft in the chili. Mince the 4 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse the 2 cans of white beans, then mash about half a can’s worth with a fork; the mashed beans thicken the chili.

Put the onion, garlic, all the beans, the 1 lb of frozen corn, the 2 small cans of mild green chiles, the 4 cups of chicken stock, the cumin, oregano and salt in the PossibleCooker pot and stir. Push the 2 lb of thawed chicken breasts under the liquid.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out.

steps: Lift the chicken onto a plate. A thermometer in the thickest piece should read at least 165°F. Shred it with two forks and stir it back in.

steps.text: Whisk a ladle of the hot broth into the yogurt in a bowl, then stir that into the pot along with the juice of the lime. Warming the yogurt first keeps it smooth. Let it stand 5 minutes with the lid on.

steps: Ladle into bowls and top with the shredded mozzarella.
tips: Canned mild green chiles add flavor, not heat; they are fine for kids.
Use thawed meat in the slow cooker, never frozen, so it heats through safely.
dinners.leftovers: It keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; cool it first and freeze flat in zip bags.
dinners.photo: A bowl of creamy white chicken chili with shredded chicken, white beans, corn and flecks of green chile, topped with melting shredded white cheese and a lime wedge.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker BBQ pulled chicken sandwiches
dinners.subtitle: Chicken breast slow-cooked until it shreds, tossed in a light barbecue sauce and piled on toasted buns with pickles.
steps: Peel the onion, slice it thin and spread it over the bottom of the PossibleCooker pot; it cooks down soft and sweet under the chicken. Lay the 2½ lb of thawed chicken breasts on top.
Whisk half the barbecue sauce (4 tablespoons) with the cider vinegar, the ½ cup of chicken stock, the garlic powder, paprika and salt, and pour it over the chicken.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out.

Check that a thermometer in the thickest piece reads at least 165°F. Shred the chicken right in the pot with two forks, stir in the remaining barbecue sauce and let it soak up the juices for 10 minutes with the lid on.
Toast the buns cut side down in a dry skillet over medium heat, about 1 minute. Pile them with the chicken and top with the pickles. A spoonful of the lime slaw on top is good too.

tips: Use thawed meat in the slow cooker, never frozen, so it heats through safely.
Lift the chicken out with a slotted spoon so the buns don’t get soggy.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: The pulled chicken keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; cool it first and freeze flat in zip bags.
dinners.photo: A toasted bun piled high with saucy shredded barbecue chicken and dill pickle chips, with creamy coleslaw and green beans on the plate.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker salsa chicken tacos
dinners.subtitle: Chicken breast slow-cooked in salsa and taco seasoning, shredded and tucked into warm corn tortillas with lettuce, cheddar and lime.
steps: Lay the 2¼ lb of thawed chicken breasts in the PossibleCooker pot. Sprinkle the packet of taco seasoning over them and pour the 16 oz of salsa on top. The salsa is all the liquid it needs.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out.

Check that a thermometer in the thickest piece reads at least 165°F. Shred the chicken in the pot with two forks and stir it into the salsa juices. Let it stand 5 minutes with the lid on to soak them up.

Warm the street-taco tortillas two or three at a time in a dry skillet over medium-high heat, 20–30 seconds per side, until soft with a few toasted spots. Stack them inside a clean kitchen towel so they stay warm and bendy.

steps: Shred the romaine heart and the cheddar. Fill three tortillas per person with chicken, lettuce and cheese, and finish with a spoonful of yogurt and a squeeze of lime.
tips: Use thawed meat in the slow cooker, never frozen, so it heats through safely.
Use a slotted spoon to fill the tacos so they don’t drip.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: The shredded chicken keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; cool it first and freeze flat in zip bags. It makes quick quesadillas and rice bowls.
dinners.photo: Corn tortilla street tacos filled with juicy shredded salsa chicken, shredded lettuce and cheddar, with a dollop of yogurt and lime wedges.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker chicken noodle soup
dinners.subtitle: Shredded chicken, carrots, celery and egg noodles in a golden broth with a squeeze of lemon.
steps: Peel the carrots and cut into coins, slice 4 ribs of celery (half a bunch), peel the onion and cut it into small dice, and mince the 3 garlic cloves.

steps.text: Take the lid off the PossibleCooker, select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to MED and press START/STOP. It preheats for about 5 minutes and beeps when it is ready for food. Add the oil, onion, carrots and celery and cook, stirring, until the onion is soft and see-through, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds. Press START/STOP to turn the heat off.

steps: Pour in the 8 cups of chicken stock (two cartons), add the Italian seasoning, salt and pepper, and push the 2 lb of thawed chicken breasts under the liquid.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out.

steps: Lift the chicken onto a plate. A thermometer in the thickest piece should read at least 165°F. Shred it with two forks.

steps.text: Take the lid off, select SEAR/SAUTÉ on HI and bring the soup to a gentle boil, about 8 minutes. Add the 6 oz of egg noodles (half a 12 oz bag) and the 6 oz of frozen peas and cook until the noodles are tender, 6–8 minutes. Stir the chicken back in, squeeze in the juice of the lemon and press START/STOP.

tips: Cook the noodles at the end, in the hot broth: noodles that slow-cook all day turn to mush.
Use thawed meat in the slow cooker, never frozen, so it heats through safely.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; the noodles keep soaking up broth, so add a splash of water when you reheat. To freeze, freeze it before the noodles go in.
dinners.photo: A bowl of chicken noodle soup with shredded chicken, wide egg noodles, carrot coins, celery and peas in a clear golden broth, a lemon wedge beside it.

dinners.title: Chicken meatballs in marinara
dinners.subtitle: Tender lean chicken meatballs simmered right in the marinara with spinach, served over spaghetti with Parmesan.
steps: In a large bowl mix the 2 lb of ground chicken with the panko, the egg, half the Parmesan, the garlic powder, the Italian seasoning and 1 teaspoon of the salt. Mix with your hands only until it comes together. With wet hands, roll it into 25 meatballs about 1½ inches across.

Pour the jar of Rao’s marinara, the can of diced tomatoes with its juice and ½ cup of water into the PossibleCooker pot and stir. Set the meatballs into the sauce in a single layer and spoon a little sauce over each.

steps.text: Put the lid on, select BRAISE, set the time to 40 minutes and press START/STOP. Leave them alone for the first 20 minutes so they firm up, then turn each one gently with a wooden spoon. They are done when a thermometer in the center of a meatball reads 165°F.

When the meatballs have about 25 minutes left, fill your largest pot with about 5 quarts of water, add 1 tablespoon of the salt, cover and bring it to a full rolling boil on the stove over high heat. It takes 10–15 minutes.

Add the 10 oz of spaghetti (a little over half a 1 lb box) to the boiling water, stir for the first minute so it doesn’t stick, and boil uncovered until tender with a little bite, 9–11 minutes (check the box). Drain.
Stir the 5 oz of spinach into the sauce around the meatballs and put the lid back on for 2 minutes, until it wilts. Serve the meatballs and sauce over the spaghetti with the rest of the Parmesan.

tips: No browning needed: simmering the meatballs in the sauce keeps lean chicken tender and saves a pan.
Don’t pack the meatballs tight; a light hand keeps them soft.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
dinners.leftovers: Meatballs in sauce keep 4 days in the fridge and freeze for 3 months; they make good hoagies with a little mozzarella.
dinners.photo: A plate of spaghetti topped with round chicken meatballs in a chunky red marinara with wilted spinach and grated Parmesan.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker beef & broccoli
dinners.subtitle: Thin strips of lean beef slow-cooked tender in a garlic-ginger soy sauce, finished with two pounds of broccoli.
steps: Slice the eye of round across the grain into thin strips, about ¼ inch thick; it is much easier while the meat is still a little frozen. Mince the 4 garlic cloves and grate the ginger.
Stir the cup of beef stock, the soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic and ginger together in the PossibleCooker pot. Add the beef and stir so every strip is in the sauce.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out. The beef is ready when a strip pulls apart easily, far past the safe 145°F.

Stir the cornstarch into 3 tablespoons of cold water and stir it into the pot. Add the 2 lb of frozen broccoli on top. Select SEAR/SAUTÉ on HI, put the lid on and cook until the broccoli is hot and bright green and the sauce has thickened, 8–10 minutes, stirring once halfway. Press START/STOP.

steps: Drizzle with the sesame oil and serve.
tips: Cut across the grain (across the lines in the meat): short fibers are what make lean beef tender.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge in a covered container; it reheats well in the microwave and is good over rice or noodles.
dinners.photo: A bowl of tender sliced beef and bright green broccoli florets in a glossy dark garlic-ginger soy sauce, with golden potstickers on the side.

dinners.title: Beef tips & gravy
dinners.subtitle: Sam’s Club beef tips slow-cooked until fork-tender with mushrooms and onions in a rich brown gravy, made for spooning over mashed potatoes.
steps: Pat the 2¼ lb of beef tips dry with paper towels and cut any big pieces down to about 1½ inches. Peel the onion and cut it into thin half-moons, slice the 8 oz of mushrooms and mince the 3 garlic cloves.

steps.text: Take the lid off the PossibleCooker, select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to HI and press START/STOP. It preheats for about 5 minutes and beeps when it is ready for food. Add the oil, then half the beef in a single layer. Brown it 3–4 minutes, turning once, and move it to a plate. Brown the second half the same way.

Add the onion and mushrooms to the pot and cook, stirring, until the onion is soft and the mushrooms have given up their liquid, 4–5 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds. Pour in the 2½ cups of beef stock and the soy sauce and scrape the browned bits off the bottom with a wooden spoon. Press START/STOP to turn the heat off.

steps: Return the beef and its juices to the pot with the Italian seasoning, salt and pepper, and stir.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 7 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 4 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out. The beef is ready when a piece pulls apart with a fork, far past the safe 145°F.

Stir the 3 tablespoons of cornstarch with 3 tablespoons of cold water in a cup until smooth. Take the lid off, select SEAR/SAUTÉ on MED and stir the cornstarch mixture into the pot. Keep stirring gently until the gravy bubbles, turns glossy and coats the back of a spoon, 3–4 minutes. Press START/STOP.

steps: Spoon the beef tips and plenty of gravy over the mashed potatoes.
tips: Portion the Sam’s pack the day you buy it: 2¼ lb to a freezer bag, pressed flat, is one dinner. Thaw a bag in the fridge overnight; frozen meat never goes straight into the slow cooker.
Dry meat browns and wet meat steams, so pat it well and brown it in two batches.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: Beef tips in gravy keep 4 days in the fridge and freeze for 3 months; cool them first and freeze flat in zip bags. Rewarm gently and serve over rice or egg noodles.
dinners.photo: Tender chunks of beef tips with sliced mushrooms and soft cooked onions in a glossy brown gravy spooned over creamy mashed potatoes, with buttered green beans beside them.

dinners.title: Air-fryer garlic steak bites & mushrooms
dinners.subtitle: Lean sirloin tip cut into bites and air-fried hot and fast with mushrooms, then tossed in a little garlic butter.
steps: Trim any silvery skin off the 2¼ lb of sirloin tip and cut the meat across the grain into 1-inch cubes. Wipe the 16 oz of mushrooms clean and cut them in half.
In a large bowl toss the steak and mushrooms with the oil, soy sauce, garlic powder, salt and black pepper. Leave them on the counter to soak up the seasoning while the air fryer heats.

steps.text: Heat the air fryer to 400°F for 3 minutes. Spread half the steak and mushrooms in the basket in a single layer and air-fry 4 minutes. Shake the basket and cook 2–4 minutes more, until the bites are browned and a thermometer in a thick piece reads 145°F. Tip them into a clean bowl and cook the second half the same way.
Add the butter to the hot steak and mushrooms and toss until it melts and coats everything. Rest 3 minutes before serving so the juices stay in the meat.

tips: Sirloin tip is lean, so stop at 145°F (medium); past that it turns chewy.
A single layer with space between the pieces browns; a crowded basket steams. Two batches are worth it.
Cut across the grain: find the lines running through the meat and cut the other way, and every bite is tender.
Portion the Sam’s roast the day you buy it: 2¼ lb to a freezer bag is one dinner, and half-thawed meat is the easiest to cube.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; good cold over a salad or warmed in a tortilla with cheese.
dinners.photo: Browned, glossy garlic-butter steak bites and halved golden mushrooms piled on a plate beside creamy smashed potatoes and bright green broccoli.

dinners.title: Pepper steak
dinners.subtitle: Thin strips of lean sirloin tip seared with lots of bell peppers and soft onions in a gingery soy gravy, for spooning over rice.
steps: Slice the 2 lb of sirloin tip across the grain into strips about ¼ inch thick and 2 inches long, and toss them with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce and 1 tablespoon of the cornstarch. Cut the 3 peppers into strips and the onion into thin half-moons. Mince the 4 garlic cloves and grate the ginger.
In a cup, stir the rest of the soy sauce and cornstarch with the cup of beef stock, the brown sugar, rice vinegar and black pepper until smooth.

steps.text: Heat half the oil in your largest skillet over high heat until it shimmers. Add half the steak in a single layer and sear without stirring for 1 minute, then stir-fry 1–2 minutes more, until browned and cooked through, past the safe 145°F. Move it to a plate and cook the second half the same way.
Add the remaining oil, the peppers and the onion to the skillet and stir-fry until the peppers are tender-crisp and the onion is soft, 4–5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce again, pour it in and return the steak and its juices. Simmer, stirring, until the gravy is glossy and coats the peppers, 1–2 minutes. Serve over the rice.

tips: Partly frozen steak slices paper-thin: 30 minutes in the freezer, or half-thawed from a freezer bag, is perfect.
Sear in two batches; a crowded pan steams the meat gray instead of browning it.
Start the rice first: the PossibleCooker’s WHITE RICE program takes about 25 minutes and holds on KEEP WARM.
Portion the Sam’s sirloin tip the day you buy it: 2 lb to a freezer bag is one dinner.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat in a skillet with a splash of water so the gravy loosens.
dinners.photo: Glossy strips of seared beef with red and green bell pepper strips and soft cooked onions in a dark soy gravy beside white jasmine rice and bright green broccoli.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker pot roast with carrots & potatoes
dinners.subtitle: A Sam’s Club chuck roast browned and slow-cooked all day with potatoes, carrots and onions until it pulls apart, with gravy made from its own juices.
steps: Pat the 2¼ lb chuck roast dry, trim off any thick outside fat and season it all over with 1½ teaspoons of the salt and the pepper. Scrub the 2 lb of potatoes and cut them into 2-inch chunks. Peel the 1½ lb of carrots and cut into 2-inch pieces. Peel the onions and cut them into wedges, and smash the 4 garlic cloves.

steps.text: Take the lid off the PossibleCooker, select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to HI and press START/STOP. It preheats for about 5 minutes and beeps when it is ready for food. Add the oil, then the roast. Brown it well, about 4 minutes a side, and move it to a plate.

Add the onion wedges and garlic and cook, stirring, until the onion starts to soften and brown, 2–3 minutes. Pour in the 2 cups of beef stock and the soy sauce and scrape the browned bits off the bottom with a wooden spoon. Press START/STOP to turn the heat off.

steps: Stir in the Italian seasoning. Set the roast back in the pot and tuck the potatoes and carrots around it; they should sit mostly in the liquid.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 8 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 5 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out. The roast is ready when it pulls apart easily with a fork, far past the safe 145°F.

Lift the roast and vegetables onto a platter with a slotted spoon and cover loosely with foil. Skim the fat off the top of the juices with a large spoon. Stir the 2 tablespoons of cornstarch with 2 tablespoons of cold water until smooth, select SEAR/SAUTÉ on MED, stir it in and keep stirring until the gravy bubbles and thickens, 3–4 minutes. Taste and add the last ½ teaspoon of salt if it needs it. Press START/STOP.

steps: Pull the roast into big chunks with two forks and serve with the potatoes and carrots, with the gravy spooned over everything.
tips: Chuck is the cut for pot roast: the long, slow cook melts it tender. Skimming the fat off the juices at the end keeps the gravy lighter.
Cut the potatoes and carrots big; small pieces turn to mush over 8 hours.
A Sam’s chuck roast runs about 3½ to 4 lb. Cut off 2¼ lb for tonight and freeze the rest, cubed, in a bag for a pot of chili.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. The meat and gravy freeze for 3 months (the potatoes turn grainy, so eat those first); shredded leftovers make good sandwiches on toasted rolls.
dinners.photo: A platter of fork-tender pot roast pulled into big chunks with large pieces of potato and carrot and soft cooked onion wedges, glossy brown gravy spooned over the top.

dinners.title: Blackstone steaks with mushrooms & onions
dinners.subtitle: A lean Sam’s sirloin tip cut into steaks, seared on a very hot griddle and sliced under a pile of browned mushrooms and golden onions.
steps: Slice the 2¼ lb of sirloin tip across the grain into 5 or 6 steaks about ¾ inch thick. Pat them dry and season both sides with the garlic powder, 1 teaspoon of the salt and the pepper. Slice the 16 oz of mushrooms and cut the onions into thin half-moons.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on high for 10 minutes; lean steak wants a very hot griddle.

Spread 1 tablespoon of the oil on one side of the griddle and add the mushrooms and onions with the rest of the salt. Cook, turning them now and then, until the onions are soft and golden and the mushrooms are browned, 8–10 minutes. Splash on the soy sauce, toss, and slide them to the coolest part.

Spread the remaining oil on the hottest part and lay the steaks down. Sear without moving them for 3 minutes, turn, and cook 2–3 minutes more, until a thermometer in the center of the thickest steak reads 145°F for medium.
Move the steaks to a cutting board, top each with a little of the butter and rest 5 minutes. Slice across the grain and serve under a pile of the mushrooms and onions.

tips: Sirloin tip is lean and best at medium (145°F); slicing it thin across the grain is what makes it tender.
Start the mushrooms and onions first: they take longer than the steaks and hold happily on the cool side.
Pat the steaks dry; a dry surface is what gets a brown crust.
A Sam’s sirloin tip roast is about 4 lb: cut what you need into steaks and freeze the rest in a 2-lb bag for pepper steak or steak bites.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; slice thin and pile on toasted rolls with the mushrooms and onions for steak sandwiches.
dinners.photo: Sliced griddle-seared steak, pink in the center, under a pile of browned mushrooms and golden caramelized onions, with crispy potato wedges and steamed broccoli, cauliflower and carrots.

dinners.title: Honey mustard chicken thighs
dinners.subtitle: Juicy boneless chicken thighs from the Sam’s tray, grilled and brushed with a sweet-tangy honey mustard.
steps: In a small bowl whisk the mustard, honey, cider vinegar and garlic powder. Spoon 3 tablespoons into a clean cup for the table.
Trim any big pieces of fat off the 2¼ lb of chicken thighs, pat them dry and toss with the oil, paprika, salt and pepper.

steps.text: Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Grill the thighs, turning once halfway and brushing with the honey mustard from the bowl during the last 2 minutes, until browned and a thermometer pushed into the thickest one reads 165°F: 10–14 minutes on an open grill, 6–8 minutes if yours closes like a press. Cook in two batches if the grill is small.
Rest the chicken 3 minutes on a clean plate, then drizzle with the honey mustard you set aside.

tips: Thighs stay juicy even a few degrees past 165°F, which makes them the forgiving choice for the grill.
Brush the sauce on at the end; honey burns if it goes on at the start.
Portion the Sam’s tray the day you buy it: 2¼ lb of thighs to a freezer bag, pressed flat, thaws overnight in the fridge.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; slice for wraps or chop over a salad.
dinners.photo: Grilled boneless chicken thighs with dark grill marks and a shiny golden honey-mustard glaze, served with a split sweet potato and garlicky green beans.

dinners.title: Chicken & vegetable stir-fry
dinners.subtitle: Strips of chicken breast and two bags of Sam’s frozen stir-fry vegetables tossed on the griddle in a light ginger-soy glaze.
steps: Cut the 2¼ lb of chicken breast into thin bite-size strips and toss with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce and 1 tablespoon of the cornstarch. Mince the 4 garlic cloves and grate the ginger.
In a cup, stir the rest of the soy sauce and cornstarch with the honey, rice vinegar and ¼ cup of water until smooth.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Spread half the oil on the griddle and cook the chicken in a single layer, turning, until golden and a thermometer in a thick piece reads 165°F, 5–7 minutes. Move it to a cooler part.

Spread the remaining oil on the hot part and pour on the 2 lb of frozen stir-fry vegetables straight from the bags. Cook, turning them every minute, until the ice has cooked off and they are hot and tender-crisp, 5–6 minutes. Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.

Toss the chicken and vegetables together, stir the sauce and pour it over. Keep tossing until it turns glossy and coats everything, about 1 minute. Drizzle with the sesame oil and serve over the rice.

tips: The stir-fry vegetables go on frozen; thawed ones turn limp.
Sam’s sells them as five 1-lb bags, so two bags are one dinner and the other three stay in the freezer.
Start the rice before you light the griddle; it holds on KEEP WARM.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; reheat in a hot skillet. Over leftover rice it makes a good packed lunch.
dinners.photo: Golden strips of chicken tossed with bright stir-fried broccoli, snap peas, carrots and red pepper strips in a glossy soy glaze beside white jasmine rice.

dinners.title: Chunky slow-cooker beef chili
dinners.subtitle: Sam’s Club stew meat cut small and slow-cooked all day with chili beans, tomatoes and peppers until every bite is tender. Made to double and freeze.
steps: Cut the 1¾ lb of stew meat into ¾-inch pieces and pat them dry. Peel the onion and cut it into small dice, dice the 2 peppers and mince the 4 garlic cloves.

steps.text: Take the lid off the PossibleCooker, select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to HI and press START/STOP. It preheats for about 5 minutes and beeps when it is ready for food. Add the oil, then half the beef in a single layer. Brown it 3–4 minutes, turning once, and move it to a plate. Brown the second half the same way.

Add the onion and peppers to the pot and cook, stirring, until the onion is soft, 4–5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, the packet of taco seasoning and the cumin for 30 seconds, then pour in the cup of beef stock and scrape up the browned bits. Press START/STOP to turn the heat off.

steps: Add the beef and its juices, the 2 cans of Bush’s chili beans with their sauce, the 2 cans of diced tomatoes with their juice and the salt, and stir.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 8 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 5 hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out. The chili is ready when the beef falls apart under a spoon, far past the safe 145°F.

steps: Stir, taste and add a pinch more salt if it needs it. Ladle into bowls and top with the shredded cheddar and a spoonful of yogurt.
tips: This is the one to double: the 6.5-quart pot holds twice the recipe, and the second half freezes flat in zip bags for a night nobody wants to cook.
Stew meat instead of ground beef gives big, tender bites; cut the pieces small so every spoonful gets one.
The pot is nonstick: stir with a wooden or silicone spoon, never metal.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; cool it first and freeze flat in zip bags. It is even better the next day over a split potato.
dinners.photo: A deep bowl of chunky beef chili with tender cubes of beef, beans, diced peppers and a thick tomato sauce, topped with shredded cheddar and a dollop of yogurt.

dinners.title: Apple-jelly glazed chicken thighs
dinners.subtitle: Grilled boneless chicken thighs brushed with the sweet-tangy apple jelly and mustard glaze from the pantry.

steps.text: In a small saucepan over low heat, melt the apple jelly with the mustard, cider vinegar and butter, stirring until smooth. Set half aside in a clean bowl for serving.

steps: Trim any big pieces of fat off the 2¼ lb of chicken thighs, pat them dry and season both sides with the salt and pepper.

steps.text: Preheat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes. Grill the thighs, turning once halfway and brushing with the glaze during the last 2 minutes, until browned and a thermometer pushed into the thickest one reads 165°F: 10–14 minutes on an open grill, 6–8 minutes if yours closes like a press.
Let the chicken rest 3 minutes on a clean plate, then spoon the reserved glaze over the top.

tips: Brush the glaze on at the end; the sugar in the jelly burns if it goes on early.
Thighs are forgiving: they stay juicy a few degrees past 165°F.
The same glaze is good on chicken breasts; pound them to an even thickness first.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; slice thin for sandwiches or wraps.
dinners.photo: Grilled boneless chicken thighs with grill marks and a shiny amber apple glaze, served with a buttered sweet potato and green beans topped with crispy fried onions.

dinners.title: Slow-cooker garlic-herb chicken with potatoes & carrots
dinners.subtitle: Chicken thighs rubbed with garlic, paprika and herbs, slow-cooked on a bed of potatoes, carrots and onions from the big Sam’s bags. No browning, one pot.
steps: Scrub the 2 lb of potatoes and cut them into 1½-inch chunks. Peel the 1½ lb of carrots and cut into 1-inch pieces. Peel the onion and cut it into wedges, and mince the 5 garlic cloves.
Put the potatoes, carrots and onion wedges in the PossibleCooker pot, toss them with half the salt and pour in the cup of chicken stock.

Trim any big pieces of fat off the 2¼ lb of chicken thighs. In a bowl, toss the chicken with the oil, garlic, Italian seasoning, paprika, pepper and the rest of the salt, and lay the pieces on top of the vegetables in an even layer.

steps.text: Put the lid on. Select SLOW COOK, set it to LO and the time to 6 hours, and press START/STOP (or use HI for 3½ hours if you are starting later in the day). Leave the lid on while it cooks; every peek lets heat out. It is done when the potatoes are tender and a thermometer in the thickest piece of chicken reads at least 165°F.

steps: Squeeze the juice of the lemon over everything. Lift the chicken and vegetables into shallow bowls with a slotted spoon and ladle some of the juices from the pot over the top.
tips: No browning and one pot: this is the dinner for a morning with ten minutes to spare.
Use thawed chicken in the slow cooker, never frozen, so it heats through safely.
Everything in it comes from the big Sam’s packs: the tray of thighs, the 10-lb bag of potatoes and the bags of carrots and onions.
When the time is up the cooker switches itself to KEEP WARM, so dinner holds if someone is running late.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge in a covered container; shred the leftover chicken into the juices and it reheats without drying out.
dinners.photo: Tender herb-rubbed chicken thighs resting on chunks of golden potato, carrot and soft cooked onion in a shallow bowl of light broth, with a lemon half beside it.

dinners.title: Hamburger steaks with onion gravy
dinners.subtitle: Seared beef patties simmered in a brown onion gravy, the diner classic made in one skillet.
steps: Divide the beef into 5 equal pieces and shape each into an oval patty about ¾ inch thick, pressing a shallow dimple into the middle so it stays flat. Season both sides with the garlic powder, salt and half the black pepper. Cut the onions in half and slice them into thin half-moons.

steps.text: Melt 1 tablespoon of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high. Brown the patties 4 minutes a side, until a deep crust forms; they finish cooking in the gravy. Move them to a plate.
Turn the heat to medium. Add the rest of the butter and the onions to the skillet and cook, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, until the onions are soft and golden, 5–6 minutes.

steps: Sprinkle the flour over the onions and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the beef broth a little at a time, stirring the whole time, until the gravy is smooth.

steps.text: Nestle the patties back into the gravy and spoon some over the top. Cover and simmer 6–8 minutes, until a thermometer in the middle of a patty reads 160°F and the gravy coats a spoon. Add the rest of the pepper and taste for salt.

tips: If the gravy gets too thick, stir in a splash of water.
Everything here is pantry and freezer food: a bag of the Sam’s ground beef, an onion and a carton of broth.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container with the gravy; reheat covered in a skillet or the microwave until hot. Freezes for up to 3 months.
dinners.photo: A seared hamburger steak smothered in glossy brown gravy and soft caramelized onions on a plate beside buttery smashed potatoes and French-style green beans.

dinners.title: Philly cheesesteaks
dinners.subtitle: Paper-thin griddled steak, soft peppers, onions and mushrooms under melted cheese on toasted hoagie rolls.
steps: Put the sirloin tip in the freezer for 15 minutes while the griddle heats; firm meat slices paper-thin. Then slice it across the grain as thin as you can. Cut the peppers and the onions into thin strips.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Cook the peppers, onions and mushrooms with 1 tablespoon of the oil on one side of the griddle, turning now and then, until soft and browned, 6–8 minutes.

Spread the steak in a thin layer on the other side with the rest of the oil and season it with the garlic powder, salt and black pepper. Cook 2–3 minutes, chopping and turning with two spatulas, until no pink remains; thin steak passes 145°F in seconds.

steps: Mix the vegetables into the steak and push it into 5 long piles. Lay the cheese slices over the piles (about 2 each, a little less for the kids) and let them melt, about 1 minute. Split the hoagie rolls, toast them cut side down on the griddle for 30 seconds, then scoop each pile into a roll with a long spatula.
tips: Partly frozen meat and a sharp knife are the whole trick to thin slices.
Provolone or American both melt well; use what the kids like.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; store the filling apart from the rolls and reheat it on the griddle or in a skillet.
dinners.photo: Toasted hoagie rolls stuffed with thin griddled steak, melted provolone, soft griddled peppers and caramelized onions, on a plate with air-fryer potato wedges and buttered corn.

dinners.title: Steak fajitas
dinners.subtitle: Lime-and-spice steak strips seared hard on the Blackstone with charred peppers and onions, in warm flour tortillas.
steps: Slice the sirloin tip across the grain into thin strips, about ¼ inch. Toss with 1 tablespoon of the oil, the taco seasoning and the juice of 1 lime. Cut the peppers and the onions into strips.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Cook the peppers and onions with the rest of the oil on one side of the griddle, turning now and then, until tender and charred at the edges, 8–10 minutes.

Sear the steak strips on the other side in a single layer without moving them for 2 minutes, then turn and cook 2–3 minutes more, until browned and 145°F. Toss with the vegetables and squeeze the second lime over everything.

steps: Warm the tortillas on a clean part of the griddle, about 15 seconds a side. Serve 2 per person with the cheddar and sour cream.
tips: Slice across the grain (the faint lines in the meat), or the strips turn out chewy.
Start the vegetables first; they take a few minutes longer than the steak.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat the filling in a skillet and use it for quesadillas or a rice bowl.
dinners.photo: Sizzling strips of seared steak with charred red and green pepper strips and griddled onions in a cast-iron pan beside warm flour tortillas, shredded cheddar and a dollop of sour cream.

dinners.title: Cheesy taco pasta
dinners.subtitle: Elbow macaroni and taco-seasoned beef in a melty cheddar and salsa sauce, ready in 25 minutes.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the elbow macaroni 1 minute less than the package says, about 6 minutes. Save ½ cup of the pasta water and drain.
While the pasta cooks, brown the beef in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F, 7–8 minutes. Drain off any fat.
Stir in the taco seasoning, the salsa and the beef broth and simmer 3 minutes.

steps: Add the drained pasta and two-thirds of the cheddar and stir until melty, adding a splash of the pasta water if it looks dry. Scatter the rest of the cheese on top, cover for a minute to melt, and serve with the sour cream.
tips: Use a mild salsa for the kids and pass hot sauce at the table.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; add a splash of water when you reheat it so it stays saucy.
dinners.photo: A skillet of elbow macaroni in a creamy, cheesy taco-seasoned beef and salsa sauce topped with melted cheddar and a dollop of sour cream, beside buttered corn and carrot sticks with ranch.

dinners.title: Mongolian beef
dinners.subtitle: Crisp-edged strips of steak in a sticky soy, brown sugar and garlic sauce over jasmine rice.
steps: Slice the sirloin tip across the grain into thin strips, about ¼ inch thick, and toss with 3 tablespoons of the cornstarch until coated. Mince the garlic and grate the ginger.
Stir the soy sauce, brown sugar, the last tablespoon of cornstarch and ½ cup of water together in a bowl for the sauce.

steps.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet over high heat until it shimmers. Sear the beef in two batches in a single layer, 1–2 minutes a side, until crisp at the edges and 145°F. Move it to a plate.

Turn the heat to medium. Add the last tablespoon of oil, the garlic and the ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Pour in the sauce and simmer, stirring, until thick and glossy, 2–3 minutes.

steps: Return the beef and toss for 1 minute to coat. Serve over the rice with the broccoli.
tips: Cook the beef in batches; a crowded pan steams the meat instead of crisping it.
Start the rice before you slice the beef so everything is ready together.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat in a skillet with a splash of water, or in the microwave.
dinners.photo: Glossy dark-brown strips of Mongolian beef in a sticky sauce over fluffy white jasmine rice with bright steamed broccoli on the side.

dinners.title: Cheesy beef quesadillas
dinners.subtitle: Taco-seasoned beef and plenty of cheddar griddled between flour tortillas until golden and melty.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.

Brown the beef on the griddle, chopping it up with a spatula, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F, 6–7 minutes. Scrape off any fat, sprinkle on the taco seasoning and 3 tablespoons of water and toss until it coats the meat.

steps: Pile the beef on one side and turn the heat to medium. Lay 5 tortillas on the griddle and cover each with a handful of cheddar, a fifth of the beef and another handful of cheese, then top with the other 5 tortillas.

steps.text: Cook until golden underneath and the cheese starts to melt, about 2 minutes, then flip with a wide spatula and cook 1–2 minutes more.

steps: Rest them a minute, cut each into 4 wedges and serve with the salsa and sour cream.
tips: Medium heat is the sweet spot: hot enough to crisp the tortilla, gentle enough to melt the cheese.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; re-crisp the wedges on the griddle or in the air fryer for a few minutes.
dinners.photo: Golden griddled quesadilla wedges oozing melted cheddar and seasoned ground beef, with small bowls of red salsa and sour cream, beside buttered Mexicorn and fresh orange wedges.

dinners.title: One-pot chili mac
dinners.subtitle: Beefy chili and elbow macaroni cooked together in one pot and finished under melted cheddar.

steps.text: In a large pot over medium-high, brown the beef with the chopped onion, breaking it up, until no pink remains, the beef reaches 160°F and the onion is soft, 7–8 minutes. Drain any fat.

steps: Stir in the cumin, paprika, garlic powder and salt for 30 seconds, then add the chili beans with their sauce, the diced tomatoes with their juice and the beef broth.

steps.text: Bring it to a boil, stir in the elbow macaroni, cover and simmer, stirring every few minutes so nothing sticks, until the pasta is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed, 10–12 minutes.

steps: Turn off the heat, scatter the cheddar over the top, cover for 2 minutes to melt and serve.
tips: If it gets too thick before the pasta is done, add a splash of water.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months in single portions; add a splash of water when you reheat it.
dinners.photo: A bowl of chili mac: elbow macaroni in a thick, beefy tomato chili sauce with beans, topped with melted cheddar, beside buttered green beans and crisp apple slices.

dinners.title: French dip sandwiches
dinners.subtitle: Thin roast beef warmed in a garlicky beef jus, piled on toasted rolls with melted cheese, with a cup of jus for dipping.

steps.text: Bring the beef broth, garlic powder and black pepper to a simmer in a saucepan; this is the jus for dipping.
Drop the roast beef into the simmering jus for 1–2 minutes, just until hot through (165°F), then lift it out with tongs and let it drip. Keep the jus warm on low.
Split the hoagie rolls, butter the cut sides and toast them cut side down in a large skillet over medium until golden, about 2 minutes.

steps: Pile the beef on the bottom halves, lay 2 cheese slices over each and put the tops on; the hot meat melts the cheese. Pour the jus into small cups for dipping.
tips: Ask the deli to shave the roast beef thin; thin slices warm through in seconds.
Anyone who doesn’t like a soggy roll can spoon the jus on instead of dipping.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; keep the beef and jus apart from the rolls and warm them together in a saucepan.
dinners.photo: A toasted hoagie roll piled with thin sliced roast beef and melted provolone, a small cup of dark beef jus for dipping, beside golden fries and buttered green beans.

dinners.title: Cheesy beef & potato skillet
dinners.subtitle: Crispy golden new potatoes and browned beef with peppers and onions, under melted cheddar.
steps: Drain the new potatoes, pat them dry and cut each into quarters. Chop the onion and the bell pepper.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add the potatoes cut side down and cook, turning once or twice, until golden and crisp at the edges, 8–10 minutes. Move them to a plate.
In the same skillet, brown the beef with the onion and bell pepper, breaking it up, until no pink remains, the beef reaches 160°F and the vegetables are soft, about 8 minutes. Drain any fat.

steps: Season with the paprika, garlic powder, salt and black pepper, return the potatoes and toss everything together.

steps.text: Scatter the cheddar over the top, cover and cook until melted, about 2 minutes.

tips: Dry potatoes brown and wet ones steam, so pat them well.
Ketchup or hot sauce on top is everyone’s own call.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat in a skillet so the potatoes crisp up again.
dinners.photo: A skillet of crispy golden potato quarters and browned ground beef with soft cooked peppers and onions under melted cheddar, beside buttered green beans and apple slices.

dinners.title: Honey garlic chicken bites
dinners.subtitle: Golden bite-size chicken tossed in a sticky honey, soy and garlic glaze, over jasmine rice.
steps: Cut the chicken into 1-inch pieces, pat them dry and toss with the cornstarch and black pepper until lightly coated. Mince the garlic. Stir the honey, soy sauce and 2 tablespoons of water together.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the chicken in a single layer, in two batches if it’s crowded, turning, until golden on all sides and 165°F in the middle, 6–8 minutes.
Turn the heat to medium-low, add the butter and garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Pour in the honey sauce and toss until it bubbles and turns sticky, about 2 minutes.

steps: Serve over the rice with the broccoli.
tips: Start the rice first; it takes about as long as everything else together.
Watch the glaze: honey goes from sticky to scorched fast, so keep the heat low once it’s in.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat in the microwave with a splash of water.
dinners.photo: Bite-size golden chicken pieces in a sticky, glossy honey garlic glaze over fluffy white rice with steamed broccoli florets.

dinners.title: Lemon pepper chicken
dinners.subtitle: Chicken breasts seared on the Blackstone with lemon zest and cracked pepper, finished in lemon butter.
steps: Pound the thick ends of the chicken breasts to an even ¾ inch between two sheets of plastic wrap. Zest 1 lemon and mix the zest with the black pepper, garlic powder and salt. Rub the chicken with the oil and season it all over.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Lay the chicken on the griddle and leave it alone 5–6 minutes, until golden and it lets go easily. Flip and cook 4–5 minutes more, until 165°F in the thickest part.

steps: Melt the butter on the griddle next to the chicken, squeeze in the juice of the zested lemon and turn the chicken through it. Rest 5 minutes, then slice. Cut the second lemon into wedges for the table.
tips: An even thickness is what keeps it juicy; don’t skip the pounding.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; slice it for salads, wraps or Jeff’s lunch.
dinners.photo: Golden seared lemon pepper chicken breasts flecked with cracked black pepper and lemon zest, lemon wedges on the side, with buttered new potatoes and French-style green beans.

dinners.title: Smothered chicken
dinners.subtitle: Thin golden chicken cutlets simmered in a creamy mushroom and onion gravy.
steps: Slice each chicken breast in half through the middle to make thin cutlets. Mix the paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper and season both sides, then dredge the cutlets in ¼ cup of the flour and shake off the extra. Slice the onion and the mushrooms.

steps.text: Heat the oil and 1 tablespoon of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high. Brown the cutlets in two batches, 3 minutes a side, until golden; they finish in the gravy. Move them to a plate.
Turn the heat to medium. Add the rest of the butter, the onion and the mushrooms and cook, scraping up the browned bits, until soft and golden, about 5 minutes.

steps: Sprinkle in the rest of the flour and stir for 1 minute, then slowly stir in the chicken broth and the milk until smooth.

steps.text: Return the chicken, spoon the gravy over it, cover and simmer until the chicken reads 165°F and the gravy has thickened, 5–6 minutes.

tips: Start the potatoes before the chicken; the gravy goes over both.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge with its gravy; reheat covered over low heat.
dinners.photo: Golden pan-fried chicken cutlets smothered in creamy mushroom gravy with soft cooked onions, beside mashed potatoes and buttered peas.

dinners.title: Chicken ranch pasta
dinners.subtitle: Penne and golden chicken in a creamy Wish-Bone ranch and cheddar sauce.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the penne 1 minute less than the package says. Save 1 cup of the pasta water and drain.

steps: While the water heats, cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and season with the garlic powder, salt and black pepper.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high and cook the chicken, turning, until golden and 165°F in the middle, 7–8 minutes.
Turn the heat to low. Stir in the milk, the Wish-Bone ranch, the cheddar and the Parmesan until smooth and melted, about 2 minutes.

steps: Add the penne and a splash of the pasta water and toss until every piece is coated.
tips: Keep the heat low once the cheese goes in, or the sauce turns grainy.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat with a splash of milk or water.
dinners.photo: Penne tossed with bite-size golden chicken in a creamy, cheesy ranch sauce dusted with Parmesan, beside steamed broccoli and crisp apple slices.

dinners.title: Southwest chicken & rice skillet
dinners.subtitle: Chicken, rice, black beans, corn and salsa simmered together in one pan and topped with cheddar.
steps: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and toss with the taco seasoning. Drain and rinse the black beans and drain the corn.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high. Cook the chicken, turning, until browned on the outside, 4–5 minutes; it finishes with the rice.

steps: Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add the chicken broth, the salsa, the beans and the corn and bring it to a boil.

steps.text: Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer without lifting the lid until the rice is tender and the chicken reads 165°F, about 18 minutes.

steps: Fluff it with a fork, scatter the cheddar over the top, cover for 2 minutes to melt and serve.
tips: Keep the lid on: the steam is what cooks the rice.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; it makes a good burrito filling the next day.
dinners.photo: A skillet of rice simmered red with salsa, with tender chicken, black beans and corn under melted cheddar, beside carrot sticks with ranch and orange wedges.

dinners.title: Hawaiian BBQ chicken
dinners.subtitle: Grilled chicken thighs glazed with a pineapple barbecue sauce, with charred pineapple over rice.
steps: Drain the pineapple chunks, saving 3 tablespoons of the juice. Stir the juice and the soy sauce into the barbecue sauce. Season the chicken thighs with the garlic powder and salt and rub them with the oil.

steps.text: Heat the electric grill on medium-high for 5 minutes.
Grill the thighs 5–6 minutes a side, until charred and 165°F. Brush them with half the sauce in the last 2 minutes.
Lay the pineapple chunks on the grill until marked, 2–3 minutes.

steps: Brush the chicken with the rest of the sauce and serve with the pineapple over the rice.
tips: Sauce goes on at the end: barbecue sauce burns if it cooks the whole time.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; chop it for a rice bowl or a quesadilla.
dinners.photo: Charred, glossy barbecue-glazed chicken thighs with grilled golden pineapple chunks over white rice, with steamed broccoli on the side.

dinners.title: Chicken tender night
dinners.subtitle: Crispy air-fried chicken tenders with barbecue, ranch and honey-mustard dips, mac & cheese and corn.

steps.text: Heat the air fryer to 400°F for 3 minutes.
Air-fry the frozen tenders in a single layer, in batches, 10–12 minutes, turning them halfway, until crisp and 165°F in the thickest one. The bag has the exact time for your brand.

steps: While they cook, stir the honey and mustard together for a honey-mustard dip, and set out the barbecue sauce and Wish-Bone ranch in small bowls.
Keep the first batch warm under a loose sheet of foil while the second batch cooks.
tips: Make the mac & cheese and corn while the tenders cook; everything lands at once.
A single layer is the difference between crispy and soggy.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; re-crisp in the air fryer at 400°F for 3–4 minutes.
dinners.photo: Golden, crispy breaded chicken tenders on a plate with small bowls of barbecue sauce, ranch and honey mustard for dipping, beside creamy stovetop mac and cheese and buttered corn.

dinners.title: Chicken street tacos
dinners.subtitle: Crispy chopped chicken thighs from the Blackstone in small flour tortillas with cheese, salsa and lime.
steps: Cut the chicken thighs into ½-inch pieces and toss them with the oil, the taco seasoning and the juice of 1 lime. Chop the cilantro.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Spread the chicken on the griddle in a single layer and leave it 3 minutes to brown, then chop and turn it with two spatulas and cook 4–5 minutes more, until crisp at the edges and 165°F.

steps: Warm the street taco tortillas on a clean part of the griddle, about 15 seconds a side, and stack them under a towel.
Fill each tortilla with chicken and top with the cheese, salsa, sour cream, cilantro and a squeeze from the second lime.
tips: Thighs stay juicy on a hot griddle; breasts work too but come off a minute sooner.
Leave the cilantro off anyone’s taco who doesn’t like it.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat the chicken on the griddle or in a skillet.
dinners.photo: Small flour street tacos filled with crispy chopped seasoned chicken, shredded cheese, a spoon of red salsa, sour cream and chopped cilantro, with lime wedges, beside black beans and buttered Mexicorn.

dinners.title: Garlic butter chicken & noodles
dinners.subtitle: Wide egg noodles and golden chicken bites in a garlic butter sauce with Parmesan.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the egg noodles until just tender, 6–7 minutes. Drain.

steps: While the water heats, cut the chicken into bite-size pieces, season with the Italian seasoning, salt and black pepper, and mince the garlic.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high and cook the chicken, turning, until golden and 165°F, about 7 minutes.
Turn the heat to medium-low. Add the butter and garlic and stir for 1 minute, then pour in the chicken broth and simmer 2 minutes.

steps: Add the noodles and the Parmesan and toss until glossy.
tips: Keep the garlic moving; it turns bitter if it browns.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat with a splash of broth or water.
dinners.photo: Wide egg noodles tossed with golden garlic butter chicken bites and grated Parmesan, beside steamed broccoli and honey-glazed carrots.

dinners.title: Chicken & dumplings
dinners.subtitle: Tender chicken, carrots and celery in a creamy broth with fluffy biscuit dumplings.
steps: Chop the onion, slice the carrots and celery thin, and cut the chicken into 1-inch pieces. Cut each biscuit into quarters.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium. Cook the onion, carrots and celery until the onion is soft, about 5 minutes. Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute.

steps: Slowly stir in the chicken broth and the milk, then add the chicken, the Italian seasoning, salt and black pepper.

steps.text: Bring it to a gentle boil, drop in the biscuit pieces one at a time, cover and simmer without lifting the lid until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through and the chicken reads 165°F, 12–15 minutes.

tips: Don’t peek: the lid holds in the steam that cooks the dumplings.
Refrigerated biscuit dough makes the dumplings; no rolling or mixing.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; the dumplings soak up broth, so add a splash of broth or water when you reheat it.
dinners.photo: A bowl of creamy chicken and dumplings with tender chicken, carrots and celery in a thick, pale gravy and fluffy dumplings, beside buttered green beans and apple slices.

dinners.title: Garlic Parmesan chicken
dinners.subtitle: Chicken breasts seared on the Blackstone and finished in garlic butter under a snow of Parmesan.
steps: Pound the thick ends of the chicken breasts to an even ¾ inch. Rub with the oil and season with the Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt and black pepper. Mince the garlic.

steps.text: Light the Blackstone and heat it on medium-high for 10 minutes; it’s ready when a few drops of water skitter and vanish in a second or two.
Lay the chicken on the griddle and leave it 5–6 minutes, until golden and it lets go easily. Flip and cook 4–5 minutes more, until 165°F in the thickest part.

steps: Melt the butter on the griddle beside the chicken, stir in the garlic for 30 seconds, and spoon the garlic butter over each piece. Shower with the Parmesan and rest 5 minutes before slicing.
tips: Add the garlic at the very end; on a hot griddle it burns in a minute.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; slice it over pasta or a salad.
dinners.photo: Seared golden chicken breasts glossy with garlic butter and a snowy layer of grated Parmesan, beside crispy air-fryer potato wedges and steamed broccoli.

dinners.title: Cheesy chicken, broccoli & rice
dinners.subtitle: Chicken, rice and broccoli cooked together in one skillet and stirred into a creamy cheddar sauce.
steps: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and season with the garlic powder, salt and black pepper.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large, deep skillet over medium-high and cook the chicken, turning, until browned on the outside, 4–5 minutes.

steps: Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add the chicken broth and bring it to a boil.

steps.text: Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Lay the frozen broccoli on top, cover again and cook 5 minutes more, until the rice is tender, the broccoli is hot and the chicken reads 165°F.

steps: Stir in the milk and the cheddar until creamy and serve.
tips: If the rice is still firm, add ¼ cup of water and give it 3 more minutes.
dinners.leftovers: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; reheat with a splash of milk.
dinners.photo: A creamy skillet of cheesy rice with tender chicken pieces and bright green broccoli florets, beside honey-glazed carrots and apple slices.

dinners.title: Fried shrimp night
dinners.subtitle: Two bags of SeaPak butterfly shrimp crisped in the air fryer, with a big pile of fries and lemon for squeezing.
steps: Make the fries first and keep them warm under a loose sheet of foil; the shrimp take about 10 minutes a batch and are best straight out of the air fryer.

steps.text: Heat the air fryer to 400°F for 3 minutes.

Spread the frozen shrimp in the basket in a single layer, with no stacking, and air-fry 9–11 minutes, shaking the basket halfway, until golden and crisp and the thickest shrimp reads 145°F. The box has the exact time for your shrimp.

steps: Tip the first batch onto a plate under the foil and cook the rest the same way.
Cut the lemon into wedges and serve the shrimp with the lemon and ketchup or cocktail sauce for dipping.
tips: Two 18 oz bags feed the five of you.
A single layer is the whole secret: stacked shrimp come out soft.
dinners.leftovers: Best right away. Leftovers keep 2 days in the fridge; re-crisp them in the air fryer at 400°F for 3–4 minutes.
dinners.photo: A plate piled with golden, crispy breaded butterfly shrimp with lemon wedges and a small cup of red cocktail sauce, beside a heap of golden fries and buttered corn.

sides.title: Air-fryer fries

steps.text: Heat the air fryer to the package temperature (usually 400°F). Cook one 26 oz bag of frozen fries (any cut) from frozen in single layers, shaking the basket halfway, until crisp and golden, about 12–18 minutes per batch.

steps: Toss with the salt while hot. Tent finished batches loosely with foil while the rest cook, then serve right away.
tips: Fries crisp in a single layer; an overfilled basket steams them soft.
sides.photo: A generous heap of golden, crispy straight-cut french fries lightly sprinkled with salt in a paper-lined basket.

sides.title: Steamed broccoli with butter
steps: Bring about ½ inch of water to a boil in a large saucepan over high heat.

steps.text: Add the 1½ lb of frozen broccoli, cover and steam over medium heat until bright green and tender-crisp, 5–7 minutes.

steps: Drain well, toss with the butter and salt, and serve.
sides.photo: A bowl of bright green steamed broccoli florets glistening with melted butter.
tips: When the PossibleCooker is free it steams this hands-off: 1 cup of water, the frozen broccoli, lid on, STEAM for 6 minutes.

sides.title: Chopped romaine salad
steps: Chop the 2 romaine hearts, rinse, spin or pat dry, and put them in a large bowl.
Whisk the juice of the lemon with the oil, salt and pepper.
Toss the salad with the dressing just before serving so it stays crisp.
sides.photo: A large bowl of crisp chopped romaine lettuce, nothing but romaine, glossy with a light lemon vinaigrette and cracked black pepper, a halved lemon beside the bowl.

sides.title: Buttered peas
steps: Bring ½ cup of water to a boil in a saucepan, add the frozen peas and cover.
Simmer until hot and tender, 3–4 minutes, then drain.
Stir in the butter and salt and serve warm.
sides.photo: A bowl of bright green sweet peas shining with melted butter.

sides.title: Buttered French-style green beans
steps: Drain the green beans and put them in a saucepan with 2 tablespoons of water.
Cover and heat over medium, stirring once or twice, until steaming, 4–5 minutes. Drain off any liquid.
Toss with the butter and black pepper and serve.
sides.photo: A bowl of tender, thin French-style green beans glossy with butter and cracked black pepper.

sides.title: Buttered sweet corn
steps: Drain the corn and put it in a saucepan with the butter.
Heat over medium, stirring, until hot and the butter coats every kernel, 3–4 minutes.
Season with the pepper and serve.
sides.photo: A bowl of golden buttered sweet corn kernels.

sides.title: Honey-glazed carrots
steps: Drain the sliced carrots well.
Melt the butter with the honey in a skillet over medium heat, add the carrots and cook, stirring gently, until hot and glazed, 4–5 minutes.
sides.photo: A bowl of shiny honey-glazed sliced carrot coins.

sides.title: Seasoned black beans
steps: Rinse and drain the black beans and put them in a saucepan with the taco seasoning and ¼ cup water.
Simmer over medium, stirring, until hot and slightly thickened, 4–5 minutes.
Squeeze the lime over the top and serve.
sides.photo: A bowl of warm seasoned black beans with a lime wedge.

sides.title: Grilled peppers & onions
steps: Quarter the 3 peppers and cut the onions into thick rounds. Brush with the oil and sprinkle with the salt.

steps.text: Grill on the preheated electric grill, turning once, until tender and charred at the edges and the onions are soft all the way through, 8–10 minutes.

steps: Slice into strips and serve warm.
sides.photo: Charred strips of red, yellow and green bell peppers and grilled onion rings with grill marks on a platter.

sides.title: Carrot sticks & ranch
steps: Scrub or peel the 1¼ lb of carrots, trim the ends and cut into sticks.
Divide among five plates with a small spoonful of ranch for dipping.
sides.photo: Bright orange carrot sticks arranged around a small bowl of creamy ranch dip.

sides.title: Crisp apple slices
steps: Wash and core the apples.
Slice just before serving so they stay bright, and divide among five plates.
sides.photo: Fanned slices of crisp red and green apples on a small plate.

sides.title: Fresh orange wedges
steps: Scrub the oranges under running water.
Cut each into 8 wedges and divide among five plates.
sides.photo: Juicy navel orange wedges arranged on a white plate.

sides.title: Air-fryer potato wedges
steps: Scrub the 2 lb of potatoes and cut into slim wedges. Toss with the oil, salt, paprika and garlic powder until evenly coated.

steps.text: Heat the air fryer to 390°F. Cook the wedges in single layers, shaking the basket halfway, until tender inside and browned outside, 18–22 minutes per batch.

steps: Tent finished batches with foil while the rest cook.
tips: Soaking the cut wedges in cold water for 10 minutes and drying them well makes them crisper.
sides.photo: Golden crispy seasoned potato wedges with browned edges piled in a bowl.

sides.title: Warm naan
steps: Heat a large dry skillet over medium heat.

steps.text: Warm each of the 3 naan 30–60 seconds per side, until soft with a few golden spots.

steps: Brush lightly with the butter and cut each into 5 wedges: three wedges a plate.
sides.photo: Warm, golden-spotted naan flatbreads brushed with butter and cut into wedges in a basket.

sides.title: Garlic toast
steps: Soften the butter and stir in the 2 minced garlic cloves.
Spread it thinly over one side of each of the 5 bread slices.

steps.text: Air-fry buttered side up at 370°F in single layers until golden and crisp at the edges, 3–5 minutes per batch. Cut each slice in half.

sides.photo: Golden, crisp slices of garlic butter toast cut into halves on a board.

sides.title: Grilled honey apples
steps: Core the apples and cut into thick wedges. Brush lightly with the oil.
Grill on a clean electric grill until marked and just tender, 3–4 minutes per side.
Drizzle with the honey and serve warm.
sides.photo: Thick apple wedges with golden grill marks drizzled with honey on a plate.

sides.title: Creamy tomato soup
steps: Combine the jar of Rao’s marinara (already fully seasoned, so no herbs are needed) and the 2 cups of chicken stock in a saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring.

steps.text: Simmer gently 10 minutes so the flavors blend.

steps: Turn the heat to low, stir in the milk and heat until steaming (don’t let it boil). Ladle into five mugs or bowls.
sides.photo: A mug of smooth, creamy orange-red tomato soup with a swirl on top.

sides.title: Buttery smashed potatoes
steps: Scrub the 2¼ lb of potatoes and cut into 1½-inch chunks (skins on). Put them in a pot, cover with cold water and add half the salt.

steps.text: Bring to a boil and simmer until a fork slides in easily, 12–15 minutes. Drain and return to the pot.

steps: Smash with the butter, milk, remaining salt and the pepper, leaving them a little chunky.
sides.photo: A bowl of rustic, buttery smashed gold potatoes with skins, topped with a melting pat of butter and black pepper.

sides.title: Warm lemon chickpeas
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas and pat dry.
Warm the oil in a skillet over medium, add the chickpeas and minced garlic and cook, stirring, until hot and lightly golden, 4–5 minutes.
Off the heat, toss with the oregano, salt and the juice of the lemon.
sides.photo: A bowl of golden warm chickpeas tossed with lemon, garlic and oregano.

sides.title: Garlic green beans

steps.text: Trim the 1½ lb of green beans. Bring ½ inch of water to a boil in a large skillet, add the beans, cover and steam until bright green and crisp-tender, 4–5 minutes. Drain the skillet.
Add the oil and butter to the skillet over medium-high heat and cook the beans, tossing, until blistered in spots, 3–4 minutes.

steps: Add the 3 minced garlic cloves and the salt and toss 30 seconds, until fragrant. Serve right away.
sides.photo: A platter of blistered fresh green beans tossed with golden sliced garlic and butter.

sides.title: Buttered corn on the cob
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Add the frozen mini ears and cook until hot and tender, 6–8 minutes (or as the package directs).
Drain, roll in the butter and sprinkle with the salt. Two ears per person.
sides.photo: Golden mini ears of sweet corn on the cob glistening with melted butter and flaky salt.

sides.title: Cilantro-lime rice
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Combine with 2¼ cups water and the salt in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 minutes. Rest, covered, 10 minutes off the heat.
Fluff with a fork and fold in the butter, the zest and juice of the lime and the chopped cilantro.
sides.photo: A bowl of fluffy white jasmine rice flecked with chopped green cilantro and lime zest, with a lime wedge.

sides.title: Steamed jasmine rice
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Combine with 2¼ cups water and the salt in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 minutes.
Rest, covered, 10 minutes off the heat, then fluff with a fork.
sides.photo: A neat mound of fluffy steamed white jasmine rice in a bowl.

sides.title: Stovetop mac & cheese
steps: Boil the macaroni in a pot of water with the salt until just tender, 7–8 minutes. Drain and return to the pot.
Whisk the cornstarch into the cold milk, pour it over the pasta with the butter and stir over medium-low heat until the milk thickens, 2–3 minutes.
Take off the heat and stir in the shredded cheddar until smooth and creamy.
sides.photo: A bowl of creamy, cheesy elbow macaroni with a glossy golden cheddar sauce.

sides.title: Sesame edamame
steps: Bring a saucepan of water to a boil, add the frozen edamame and cook until hot and tender, 4–5 minutes.
Drain and toss with the sesame oil and salt.
sides.photo: A bowl of bright green shelled edamame beans glistening with sesame oil and flaky salt.

sides.title: Crispy potstickers

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 15 frozen potstickers flat side down and cook until the bottoms are golden, about 2 minutes.
Carefully add ½ cup of water (it spatters), cover right away and steam until the water is gone and the filling is hot, 6–8 minutes (follow the package if it differs).

steps: Uncover and cook 1 minute more to re-crisp. Stir the soy sauce and rice vinegar together for dipping. Three per person.
sides.photo: Golden pan-fried potstickers with crispy browned bottoms arranged on a plate with a small bowl of soy dipping sauce.

sides.title: Chilled pineapple chunks
steps: Chill the cans ahead of time if you can.
Drain the pineapple chunks and divide among five small bowls.
sides.photo: A bowl of juicy golden pineapple chunks.

sides.title: Smoky pork & beans
steps: Empty the pork and beans into a saucepan and stir in the barbecue sauce and mustard.

steps.text: Simmer over medium-low heat, stirring often, until thick and bubbling, 8–10 minutes.

sides.photo: A bowl of thick, saucy barbecue-style beans in a glossy brown sauce.

sides.title: Tortilla chips & salsa
steps: Pour the chips into a bowl (about a handful each) and the salsa into a smaller one for dipping.
sides.photo: A basket of golden tortilla chips beside a small bowl of smooth red jarred salsa.

sides.title: Cajun skillet potatoes
steps: Drain the Del Monte Cajun-style diced potatoes well and pat them dry so they brown instead of steam.
Melt the butter in your largest skillet over medium-high. Spread the potatoes in one layer and cook 8–10 minutes, stirring only every few minutes, until browned and crisp at the edges.
They’re already seasoned, so taste before adding any salt.
sides.photo: Golden, crisp-edged diced Cajun potatoes flecked with red pepper and spices in a cast-iron skillet.

sides.title: Golden turmeric rice
steps: Rinse the 1½ cups of basmati rice in a strainer until the water runs mostly clear.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the turmeric for 30 seconds, then add the rice, 2¼ cups of water and the salt. Bring to a boil.

steps.text: Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer 15 minutes without lifting the lid. Rest 5 minutes with the lid on, then fluff with a fork. Short on time? Microwave basmati rice pouches and stir in the turmeric butter instead.

sides.photo: A bowl of fluffy golden-yellow turmeric basmati rice with separate long grains and a small pat of butter.

sides.title: Old Bay air-fryer fries
steps: Air-fry one 26 oz bag of frozen fries from frozen at the package temperature (usually 400°F) in single layers, shaking the basket halfway, until crisp and golden, about 12–18 minutes per batch.
Toss the hot fries in a big bowl with the Old Bay seasoning. It’s salty, so skip any other salt.
sides.photo: Crispy golden french fries dusted with reddish Old Bay-style seasoning in a paper-lined basket.

sides.title: Cajun air-fryer fries
steps: Air-fry one 26 oz bag of frozen fries from frozen at the package temperature (usually 400°F) in single layers, shaking the basket halfway, until crisp and golden, about 12–18 minutes per batch.
Toss the hot fries with the Slap Ya Mama Cajun seasoning right away so it sticks. It’s salty, so skip any other salt.
sides.photo: Crispy french fries tossed with orange-red Cajun spice seasoning in a metal basket lined with paper.

sides.title: Green beans with crispy onions
