steps: Drain the canned green beans and warm them with the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, 4–5 minutes.
Season with the black pepper, pour into a serving bowl and scatter the French’s crispy fried onions over the top right before serving so they stay crunchy.
sides.photo: A serving bowl of buttered green beans topped with a crunchy pile of golden crispy fried onions.

sides.title: Charro beans
steps: Empty the La Preferida charro beans and their broth into a saucepan.
Warm over medium, stirring now and then, until bubbling, 6–8 minutes. They’re already seasoned, so nothing else goes in.
sides.photo: A bowl of brothy Mexican charro beans: pinto beans simmered with bits of bacon and jalapeño in a light tomato broth.

sides.title: Steamed carrots with butter
steps: Peel the 1½ lb of carrots and cut into ½-inch coins.

steps.text: Pour 1 cup of water into the PossibleCooker pot, add the carrots and put the lid on. Select STEAM, set the time to 9 minutes and press START/STOP. The cooker brings the water to a boil first, then counts the time down and beeps. The carrots are done when a fork slides into a coin easily.

steps: Drain well, toss with the butter and salt, and serve.
tips: STEAM heats the water to a boil before its timer starts, so the time you set is all cooking time. Thick coins may want 2 minutes more.
sides.photo: A bowl of bright orange steamed carrot coins glistening with a little melted butter.

sides.title: Steamed green beans with lemon
steps: Trim the stem ends off the 1½ lb of green beans.

steps.text: Pour 1 cup of water into the PossibleCooker pot, add the beans and put the lid on. Select STEAM, set the time to 7 minutes and press START/STOP. The cooker brings the water to a boil first, then counts the time down and beeps. The beans are done when they are bright green and bend without snapping.

steps: Drain well and toss with the butter, the salt and the juice of half the lemon. Cut the other half into wedges for the table.
tips: STEAM heats the water to a boil before its timer starts, so the time you set is all cooking time.
sides.photo: A platter of bright green steamed whole green beans glistening with butter, with lemon wedges.

sides.title: PossibleCooker jasmine rice
steps: Rinse the 1½ cups of jasmine rice in a fine strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.

steps.text: Put the rice, the salt and 2¼ cups of water in the PossibleCooker pot. (Ninja’s ratio is 1½ cups of water for each cup of white rice; the lines inside the pot mark it for whole cups.) Put the lid on, select WHITE RICE and press START/STOP. The cooker sets the time itself, about 25 minutes, and switches to KEEP WARM when the rice is done.

steps: Fluff with the rice paddle and serve.
tips: It holds on KEEP WARM until everything else is ready, which makes it the easy way to time a rice dinner.
sides.photo: A neat mound of fluffy steamed white jasmine rice in a bowl with a rice paddle.

sides.title: Lighter mashed potatoes
steps: Peel the 2¼ lb of potatoes and cut into 1-inch chunks.

steps.text: Put the potatoes in the PossibleCooker pot with enough cold water to just cover them (about 6 cups) and half the salt. Put the lid on, select SEAR/SAUTÉ, set it to HI and press START/STOP. It comes to a boil in about 12 minutes.
Set the lid a little ajar and boil gently until a chunk falls apart under a fork, 12–15 minutes. Press START/STOP.

steps: Lift the pot out by its handles with pot holders and drain the potatoes in a colander, then tip them back into the pot. Mash with a silicone or wooden masher (the pot is nonstick) and stir in the ½ cup of chicken stock, the yogurt, butter, pepper and the rest of the salt until creamy.
tips: Yogurt and a little stock make them creamy with a quarter of the usual butter.
Warm the stock for 30 seconds in the microwave so the potatoes stay hot.
sides.photo: A bowl of creamy mashed potatoes with a small pat of melting butter and cracked black pepper.

sides.title: Steamed broccoli, cauliflower & carrots

steps.text: Pour 1 cup of water into the PossibleCooker pot, add the 1½ lb of frozen Normandy blend (broccoli, cauliflower and carrots) straight from the bag and put the lid on. Select STEAM, set the time to 7 minutes and press START/STOP. The cooker brings the water to a boil first, then counts the time down and beeps.

steps: Drain well and toss with the butter, salt and pepper.
tips: The 4-lb Sam’s bag is nearly three dinners’ worth: pour out what you need and put the bag straight back in the freezer.
If the cooker is busy with the main dish, ½ inch of boiling water in a covered pan on the stove does the same job in 5–7 minutes.
sides.photo: A bowl of steamed broccoli florets, cauliflower florets and crinkle-cut carrot slices glistening with a little melted butter.

sides.title: Buttered Mexicorn
steps: Drain the Mexicorn and put it in a saucepan with 2 tablespoons of water.

steps.text: Heat over medium, stirring once or twice, until steaming, 4–5 minutes.

steps: Stir in the butter and the black pepper and serve.
sides.photo: A bowl of golden Mexicorn, sweet corn kernels with little pieces of red and green bell pepper, glossy with melted butter.

sides.title: Buttered new potatoes
steps: Drain the new potatoes and cut any big ones in half.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a skillet over medium-high, add the potatoes and cook, shaking the pan now and then, until golden in spots and hot through, 8–10 minutes.

steps: Sprinkle with the garlic powder, Italian seasoning, salt and black pepper, toss and serve.
sides.photo: A bowl of small golden whole new potatoes glossy with butter and flecked with herbs and cracked black pepper.
